Require Import Base.
Require Import LibExtra.
Require Import Coq.Lists.List.
Require Import AbstractSyntax PreTyping Typing GeneralTyping RecordTypes InertTypes DefRecordInertTyping HeapCorrespondence OperationalSemantics Effects Initialization InitTyping InitLookup ConfigTyping.
Require Import CommittedSubHeap FreeSubHeapSingle FreeSubHeapStack StackTyping InertInitContexts InitWeakening EffectCorrespondence HeapEffects HeapDefsPointsTo WellPointed FreeItems PreciseTyping HeapUpdate.
Unset Implicit Arguments.

(* ==================================================================== *)
(* Restricted statement under investigation.                            *)
(* ==================================================================== *)

Definition field_lookup_sub_record_statement (a : trm_label) : Prop :=
  forall (G:ctx) (V:typ) (Tf S U:typ),
    record_type V ->
    record_has V (dec_trm a Tf Tf) ->
    G ⊢ V <: typ_rcd (dec_trm a S U) ->
    G ⊢ Tf <: U.

(* ==================================================================== *)
(* A variable name; [var] is an abstract parameter, but [var_fresh]     *)
(* provides one.  The term label [a] and the type-member label [A] are  *)
(* abstract parameters too; the refutation below is parametric in them. *)
(* ==================================================================== *)

Definition x0 : var := proj1_sig (var_fresh \{}).

(* ==================================================================== *)
(* A soundness interpretation of types for the fixed context            *)
(*   G0 = x0 : typ_rcd (dec_typ A V Targ)                               *)
(* where V and Targ are closed record types.  The interpretation is     *)
(* the same simple one used in FieldSub.v: only [typ_bot] is false.     *)
(* ==================================================================== *)

Fixpoint interp (T:typ) : Prop :=
  match T with
  | typ_top => True
  | typ_bot => False
  | typ_rcd _ => True
  | typ_and T U => interp T /\ interp U
  | typ_sel _ _ => True
  | typ_bnd _ => True
  | typ_all _ _ => True
  | typ_con _ _ _ => True
  end.

(* [Inv T] records that a type is a "safe" type for the variable [x0]:
   it is true under [interp], every record type member [dec_typ] has a
   safe upper bound, and bound types are recursively safe at their
   opening.  It has no constructor for [typ_bot]. *)

Inductive Inv : typ -> Prop :=
| inv_top : Inv typ_top
| inv_rcd_trm : forall (a:trm_label) (S U:typ),
    Inv (typ_rcd (dec_trm a S U))
| inv_rcd_typ : forall (A:typ_label) (S T:typ),
    Inv T -> Inv (typ_rcd (dec_typ A S T))
| inv_and : forall (T U:typ),
    Inv T -> Inv U -> Inv (typ_and T U)
| inv_sel : forall (x:avar) (A:typ_label),
    Inv (typ_sel x A)
| inv_bnd : forall (T:typ),
    Inv (open x0 T) -> Inv (typ_bnd T)
| inv_all : forall (S T:typ), Inv (typ_all S T)
| inv_con : forall (Ts:typs) (is':inits) (T:typ),
    Inv (typ_con Ts is' T).

Lemma Inv_sound : forall (T:typ), Inv T -> interp T.
Proof.
  intros T H. induction H; cbn [interp]; auto.
Qed.

Lemma Inv_rcd_typ_inv : forall (A:typ_label) (S T:typ),
  Inv (typ_rcd (dec_typ A S T)) -> Inv T.
Proof.
  intros A S T H. inversion H; subst; assumption.
Qed.

Lemma Inv_bnd_inv : forall (T:typ),
  Inv (typ_bnd T) -> Inv (open x0 T).
Proof.
  intros T H. inversion H; subst; assumption.
Qed.

Lemma Inv_not_bot : forall (T:typ), T = typ_bot -> Inv T -> False.
Proof.
  intros T E H. subst T. inversion H.
Qed.

Lemma trm_var_eq : forall (x y:var),
  trm_var (avar_f x) = trm_var (avar_f y) -> x = y.
Proof.
  intros x y E. inversion E; subst; reflexivity.
Qed.

Section Counterexample.

Variables (a : trm_label) (A : typ_label) (S0 : typ).

(* The source record type: a genuine [record_type] (indeed a closed one). *)
Definition Vc : typ := typ_rcd (dec_trm a typ_top typ_top).

(* The target record type; its upper bound is fixed to [typ_bot], while  *)
(* its lower bound [S0] is a parameter (needed for the S = U variant).    *)
Definition Targc : typ := typ_rcd (dec_trm a S0 typ_bot).

(* The (bad-bounds) binding of [x0]. *)
Definition RVc : typ := typ_rcd (dec_typ A Vc Targc).

Definition Gc : ctx := x0 ~ RVc.

Lemma record_type_Vc : record_type Vc.
Proof.
  unfold Vc.
  exists (\{label_trm a}).
  eapply rt_one.
  - apply rd_trm.
  - reflexivity.
Qed.

Lemma record_has_Vc : record_has Vc (dec_trm a typ_top typ_top).
Proof.
  unfold Vc. apply rh_one.
Qed.

Lemma binds_Gc : binds x0 RVc Gc.
Proof. unfold Gc. apply binds_single_eq. Qed.

(* Vc <: x0.A via sel2, and x0.A <: Targc via sel1, hence Vc <: Targc. *)
Lemma sub_Vc_Targc : Gc ⊢ Vc <: Targc.
Proof.
  eapply subtyp_trans with (T := typ_sel (avar_f x0) A).
  - eapply subtyp_sel2. apply ty_var. exact binds_Gc.
  - eapply subtyp_sel1. apply ty_var. exact binds_Gc.
Qed.

(* ==================================================================== *)
(* Main soundness/typing-invariant induction for the context [Gc].      *)
(* ==================================================================== *)

Lemma Gc_typing_sub_sound :
  (forall (G:ctx) (t:trm) (T:typ), G ⊢ t ∶ T ->
     G = Gc -> forall y, t = trm_var (avar_f y) -> y = x0 /\ Inv T) /\
  (forall (G:ctx) (l:lit) (T:typ), G ⊢ l ∶ T -> True) /\
  (forall (G:ctx) (S U:typ), G ⊢ S <: U ->
     G = Gc -> (interp S -> interp U) /\ (Inv S -> Inv U)) /\
  (forall (G:ctx) (avs:avars) (Ts:typs), G ⊢ avs :: Ts -> True).
Proof.
  apply (rules_mutind
    (fun (G:ctx) (t:trm) (T:typ) (_:G ⊢ t ∶ T) =>
       G = Gc -> forall y, t = trm_var (avar_f y) -> y = x0 /\ Inv T)
    (fun (G:ctx) (l:lit) (T:typ) (_:G ⊢ l ∶ T) => True)
    (fun (G:ctx) (S U:typ) (_:G ⊢ S <: U) =>
       G = Gc -> (interp S -> interp U) /\ (Inv S -> Inv U))
    (fun (G:ctx) (avs:avars) (Ts:typs) (_:G ⊢ avs :: Ts) => True)).
  - (* ty_var *)
    intros G x T b H y E. subst G.
    assert (Exy : x = y) by (apply trm_var_eq; exact E). subst y.
    apply binds_single_inv in b. destruct b as [Ex ET].
    subst x. subst T.
    split.
    + reflexivity.
    + apply inv_rcd_typ, inv_rcd_trm.
  - (* ty_all_elim *) intros G x z S T p IH1 p2 IH2 H y E. discriminate E.
  - (* ty_new *) intros G x avs xs Ts is' T p IH1 p2 IH2 p3 H y E. discriminate E.
  - (* ty_rcd_elim *) intros G x a0 S T p IH1 H y E. discriminate E.
  - (* ty_fld_asn *) intros G x y0 a0 S T p IH1 p2 IH2 H y E. discriminate E.
  - (* ty_let *) intros L G t u T U p IH1 p2 IH2 H y E. discriminate E.
  - (* ty_llit *) intros L G l u T U p IH1 p2 IH2 H y E. discriminate E.
  - (* ty_rec_intro *)
    intros G x T p IH H y E.
    assert (Exy : x = y) by (apply trm_var_eq; exact E). subst y.
    destruct (IH H x eq_refl) as [Ex Hinv].
    subst x. split; [reflexivity | apply inv_bnd; exact Hinv].
  - (* ty_rec_elim *)
    intros G x T p IH H y E.
    assert (Exy : x = y) by (apply trm_var_eq; exact E). subst y.
    destruct (IH H x eq_refl) as [Ex Hinv].
    subst x. split; [reflexivity | apply Inv_bnd_inv in Hinv; exact Hinv].
  - (* ty_and_intro *)
    intros G x T U p IH1 p2 IH2 H y E.
    assert (Exy : x = y) by (apply trm_var_eq; exact E). subst y.
    destruct (IH1 H x eq_refl) as [Ex Hinv1].
    destruct (IH2 H x eq_refl) as [_ Hinv2].
    subst x. split; [reflexivity | apply inv_and; assumption].
  - (* ty_sub *)
    intros G t T U p IH1 s IH2 H y E.
    destruct (IH1 H y E) as [Ex HinvT].
    split; [exact Ex | apply (proj2 (IH2 H)); exact HinvT].
  - (* ty_all_intro *) intros; exact I.
  - (* ty_con_intro *) intros; exact I.
  - (* subtyp_top *)
    intros G T H. split; [intros _; exact I | intros _; apply inv_top].
  - (* subtyp_bot *)
    intros G T H. split.
    + intros HI. cbn [interp] in HI. destruct HI.
    + intros HI. inversion HI.
  - (* subtyp_refl *)
    intros G T H. split; intros; assumption.
  - (* subtyp_trans *)
    intros G S T U s IH1 s0 IH2 H.
    destruct (IH1 H) as [Hi1 Hi2]. destruct (IH2 H) as [Hj1 Hj2].
    split; intros; [apply Hj1, Hi1 | apply Hj2, Hi2]; assumption.
  - (* subtyp_and11 *)
    intros G T U H. split.
    + intros HI. cbn [interp] in HI. tauto.
    + intros HI. inversion HI; subst; assumption.
  - (* subtyp_and12 *)
    intros G T U H. split.
    + intros HI. cbn [interp] in HI. tauto.
    + intros HI. inversion HI; subst; assumption.
  - (* subtyp_and2 *)
    intros G S T U s IH1 s0 IH2 H.
    destruct (IH1 H) as [Hi1 Hi2]. destruct (IH2 H) as [Hj1 Hj2].
    split.
    + intros HS. split; [apply Hi1 | apply Hj1]; exact HS.
    + intros HS. apply inv_and; [apply Hi2 | apply Hj2]; exact HS.
  - (* subtyp_fld *)
    intros G a0 T1 T2 U1 U2 s IH1 s0 IH2 H.
    split; intros; [exact I | apply inv_rcd_trm].
  - (* subtyp_typ *)
    intros G A0 S1 T1 S2 T2 s IH1 s0 IH2 H.
    split.
    + intros _; exact I.
    + intros HI. apply Inv_rcd_typ_inv in HI.
      apply inv_rcd_typ. apply (proj2 (IH2 H)). exact HI.
  - (* subtyp_sel2 *)
    intros G x A0 S T p IHty H.
    split; intros; [exact I | apply inv_sel].
  - (* subtyp_sel1 *)
    intros G x A0 S T p IHty H.
    destruct (IHty H x eq_refl) as [_ Hinv].
    apply Inv_rcd_typ_inv in Hinv.
    split; intros; [apply Inv_sound; exact Hinv | exact Hinv].
  - (* subtyp_all *)
    intros L G S1 T1 S2 T2 s IH1 s0 IH2 H.
    split; intros; [exact I | apply inv_all].
  - (* typ_avars_nil *) intros; exact I.
  - (* typ_avars_cons *) intros; exact I.
Qed.

(* In [Gc] the empty-bounds subtyping [top <: bot] is not derivable. *)
Lemma Gc_not_top_sub_bot : ~ (Gc ⊢ typ_top <: typ_bot).
Proof.
  intro Hsub.
  pose proof (proj1 (proj2 (proj2 (Gc_typing_sub_sound)))
                Gc typ_top typ_bot Hsub eq_refl) as Hconj.
  destruct Hconj as [Hi _].
  cbn [interp] in Hi.
  exact (Hi I).
Qed.

(* ==================================================================== *)
(* The counterexample refutes the restricted statement.                 *)
(* ==================================================================== *)

Theorem field_lookup_sub_record_refuted :
  ~ field_lookup_sub_record_statement a.
Proof.
  intro Hstmt.
  specialize (Hstmt Gc Vc typ_top S0 typ_bot).
  assert (Hconc : Gc ⊢ typ_top <: typ_bot).
  { eapply Hstmt.
    - exact record_type_Vc.
    - exact record_has_Vc.
    - exact sub_Vc_Targc. }
  exact (Gc_not_top_sub_bot Hconc).
Qed.

End Counterexample.

(* The statement fails for every term-label and every element of the    *)
(* abstract type-label parameter (which is what is needed to build a    *)
(* context with a type member).                                         *)
Theorem field_lookup_sub_record_refuted_all :
  forall (a : trm_label) (A : typ_label),
    ~ field_lookup_sub_record_statement a.
Proof.
  intros a A. exact (field_lookup_sub_record_refuted a A typ_top).
Qed.

(* ==================================================================== *)
(* Variant: the target record has equal bounds (S = U).  The same       *)
(* bad-bounds context refutes it.                                       *)
(* ==================================================================== *)

Definition field_lookup_sub_record_eq_statement (a : trm_label) : Prop :=
  forall (G:ctx) (V:typ) (Tf S:typ),
    record_type V ->
    record_has V (dec_trm a Tf Tf) ->
    G ⊢ V <: typ_rcd (dec_trm a S S) ->
    G ⊢ Tf <: S.

Theorem field_lookup_sub_record_eq_refuted :
  forall (a : trm_label) (A : typ_label),
    ~ field_lookup_sub_record_eq_statement a.
Proof.
  intros a A Hstmt.
  specialize (Hstmt (Gc a A typ_bot) (Vc a) typ_top typ_bot).
  assert (Hconc : Gc a A typ_bot ⊢ typ_top <: typ_bot).
  { eapply Hstmt.
    - exact (record_type_Vc a).
    - exact (record_has_Vc a).
    - exact (sub_Vc_Targc a A typ_bot). }
  exact (Gc_not_top_sub_bot a A typ_bot Hconc).
Qed.

(* ==================================================================== *)
(* Variant: [rc V] (closure of records/top under intersections) instead *)
(* of [record_type V].  This hypothesis is weaker, and the same         *)
(* counterexample satisfies it.                                         *)
(* ==================================================================== *)

Inductive rc : typ -> Prop :=
| rc_top : rc typ_top
| rc_rcd : forall (D:dec), rc (typ_rcd D)
| rc_and : forall (T U:typ), rc T -> rc U -> rc (typ_and T U).

Definition field_lookup_sub_rc_statement (a : trm_label) : Prop :=
  forall (G:ctx) (V:typ) (Tf S U:typ),
    rc V ->
    record_has V (dec_trm a Tf Tf) ->
    G ⊢ V <: typ_rcd (dec_trm a S U) ->
    G ⊢ Tf <: U.

Lemma rc_Vc : forall (a:trm_label), rc (Vc a).
Proof. intros a. unfold Vc. apply rc_rcd. Qed.

Theorem field_lookup_sub_rc_refuted :
  forall (a : trm_label) (A : typ_label),
    ~ field_lookup_sub_rc_statement a.
Proof.
  intros a A Hstmt.
  specialize (Hstmt (Gc a A typ_top) (Vc a) typ_top typ_top typ_bot).
  assert (Hconc : Gc a A typ_top ⊢ typ_top <: typ_bot).
  { eapply Hstmt.
    - exact (rc_Vc a).
    - exact (record_has_Vc a).
    - exact (sub_Vc_Targc a A typ_top). }
  exact (Gc_not_top_sub_bot a A typ_top Hconc).
Qed.

Set Implicit Arguments.

Require Import LibExtra.

Require Import Coq.Program.Equality.

Require Import AbstractSyntax RecordTypes.

Inductive inert_typ : typ -> Prop :=
  | inert_typ_all : forall S T, inert_typ (typ_all S T)
  | inert_typ_con :
      forall Ts is' T,
        record_type T ->
        inert_typ (typ_con Ts is' T)
  | inert_typ_bnd : forall T,
      record_type T ->
      inert_typ (typ_bnd T).

Inductive inert : ctx -> Prop :=
  | inert_empty : inert empty
  | inert_all : forall G x T,
      inert G ->
      inert_typ T ->
      x # G ->
      inert (G & x ~ T).
===== RECORD TYPES =====
Set Implicit Arguments.

Require Import LibExtra.

Require Import Coq.Program.Equality.

Require Import AbstractSyntax Typing.

Implicit Types (ds : defs) (hds : heap_defs).

Inductive record_dec : dec -> Prop :=
| rd_typ : forall A T, record_dec (dec_typ A T T)
| rd_trm : forall a T, record_dec (dec_trm a T T).

Inductive record_typ : typ -> fset label -> Prop :=
| rt_one : forall D l,
  record_dec D ->
  l = label_of D ->
  record_typ (typ_rcd D) \{l}
| rt_cons: forall T ls D l,
  record_typ T ls ->
  record_dec D ->
  l = label_of D ->
  l \notin ls ->
  record_typ (typ_and T (typ_rcd D)) (union ls \{l}).

Definition record_type T := exists ls, record_typ T ls.

Inductive record_has: typ -> dec -> Prop :=
| rh_one : forall D,
    record_has (typ_rcd D) D
| rh_andl : forall T U D,
    record_has T D ->
    record_has (typ_and T U) D
| rh_andr : forall T U D,
    record_has U D ->
    record_has (typ_and T U) D.

Section HasntNotIn.

Context {A : Set} `{LA : LabelOf A} `{DTA : DecTyping A}.

Context {DTL : DecTypingLabels DTA}.

End HasntNotIn.

Section RecordHasTyDefs.

Context {A : Set} `{LA : LabelOf A} `{DTA : DecTyping A}.

End RecordHasTyDefs.

Set Implicit Arguments.

Require Import LibExtra.

Require Import Coq.Program.Equality.

Require Import AbstractSyntax.

Reserved Notation "G '⊢!' x '∶' T '⪼' U" (at level 40, x at level 59).

Inductive precise_flow : var -> ctx -> typ -> typ -> Prop :=

  | pf_bind : forall x G T,
      binds x T G ->
      G ⊢! x ∶ T ⪼ T

  | pf_open : forall x G T U,
      G ⊢! x ∶ T ⪼ typ_bnd U ->
      G ⊢! x ∶ T ⪼ open x U

  | pf_and1 : forall x G T U1 U2,
      G ⊢! x ∶ T ⪼ typ_and U1 U2 ->
      G ⊢! x ∶ T ⪼ U1

  | pf_and2 : forall x G T U1 U2,
      G ⊢! x ∶ T ⪼ typ_and U1 U2 ->
      G ⊢! x ∶ T ⪼ U2

where "G '⊢!' x '∶' T '⪼' U" := (precise_flow x G T U).
====PRETYPING====
Set Implicit Arguments.

Require Import LibExtra AbstractSyntax.

Class PreTyping {B : Set} {A : Set} (ty_rel : ctx -> A -> B -> Prop).

Class PreTypingWeakenMiddle {A : Set} {B : Set}
      {ty_rel : ctx -> A -> B -> Prop} (PTy : PreTyping ty_rel) :=
  weaken_middle : forall Gamma1 x T' Gamma2 t T,
      ty_rel (Gamma1 & Gamma2) t T ->
      x # Gamma1 ->
      ty_rel (Gamma1 & x ~ T' & Gamma2) t T.

Class PreTypingBndIntroMiddle {A : Set} {B : Set}
      {ty_rel : ctx -> A -> B -> Prop} (PTy : PreTyping ty_rel) :=
  bnd_intro_middle : forall Gamma1 Gamma2 y T1 t T,
    ty_rel (Gamma1 & y ~ open y T1 & Gamma2) t T ->
    ty_rel (Gamma1 & y ~ typ_bnd T1 & Gamma2) t T.

Section Weakening.

Context {B : Set} {A : Set} {ty_rel : ctx -> A -> B -> Prop}.

Context {PTy : PreTyping ty_rel} {PTyWM : PreTypingWeakenMiddle PTy}.

End Weakening.

Section BndIntro.

Context {B : Set} {A : Set} {ty_rel : ctx -> A -> B -> Prop}.

Context {PTy : PreTyping ty_rel} {PTyWM : PreTypingBndIntroMiddle PTy}.

End BndIntro.

Set Implicit Arguments.

Require Import LibExtra AbstractSyntax PreTyping Typing.

Implicit Types (Gamma G : ctx) (T U : typ) (x y z : var) (t : trm).

Inductive ty_def : DecTyping def :=

| ty_def_typ : forall G A T,
    G ⊢ def_typ A T ∶d dec_typ A T T

| ty_def_trm : forall G a t T,
    G ⊢ def_trm a ∶d dec_trm a T T.

Existing Instance ty_def.

Inductive ty_trm : Typing trm :=

| ty_var : forall G x T,
    binds x T G ->
    G ⊢ trm_var (avar_f x) ∶ T

| ty_all_elim : forall G x z S T,
    G ⊢ trm_var (avar_f x) ∶ typ_all S T ->
    G ⊢ trm_var (avar_f z) ∶ S ->
    G ⊢ trm_app (avar_f x) (avar_f z) ∶ open z T

| ty_new : forall G x avs xs Ts is' T,
    G ⊢ trm_var (avar_f x) ∶ typ_con Ts is' T ->
    G ⊢ avs :: Ts ->
    vars_of_avars xs avs ->
    G ⊢ trm_new (avar_f x) avs ∶ typ_bnd (open_rec_vars 1 xs T)

| ty_rcd_elim : forall G x a S T,
    G ⊢ trm_var (avar_f x) ∶ typ_rcd (dec_trm a S T) ->
    G ⊢ trm_sel (avar_f x) a ∶ T

| ty_fld_asn : forall G x y a S T,
    G ⊢ trm_var (avar_f x) ∶ typ_rcd (dec_trm a S T) ->
    G ⊢ trm_var (avar_f y) ∶ S ->
    G ⊢ trm_asn (avar_f x) a (avar_f y) ∶ T

| ty_let : forall L G t u T U,
    G ⊢ t ∶ T ->
    (forall x, x \notin L ->
      G & x ~ T ⊢ open x u ∶ U) ->
    G ⊢ trm_let T t u ∶ U

| ty_llit : forall L G l u T U,
    G ⊢ l ∶ T ->
    (forall x, x \notin L ->
      G & x ~ T ⊢ open x u ∶ U) ->
    G ⊢ trm_lit T l u ∶ U

| ty_rec_intro : forall G x T,
    G ⊢ trm_var (avar_f x) ∶ open x T ->
    G ⊢ trm_var (avar_f x) ∶ typ_bnd T

| ty_rec_elim : forall G x T,
    G ⊢ trm_var (avar_f x) ∶ typ_bnd T ->
    G ⊢ trm_var (avar_f x) ∶ open x T

| ty_and_intro : forall G x T U,
    G ⊢ trm_var (avar_f x) ∶ T ->
    G ⊢ trm_var (avar_f x) ∶ U ->
    G ⊢ trm_var (avar_f x) ∶ typ_and T U

| ty_sub : forall G (t : trm) T U,
    G ⊢ t ∶ T ->
    G ⊢ T <: U ->
    G ⊢ t ∶ U

with ty_lit : Typing lit :=

| ty_all_intro : forall L G T t U,
    (forall x, x \notin L ->
      G & x ~ T ⊢ open x t ∶ open x U) ->
    G ⊢ lit_fun T t ∶ typ_all T U

| ty_con_intro : forall L G Ts is' T ds t T',
    (forall x ys,
        length ys = length_s Ts ->
        fresh L (S (length ys)) (cons x ys) ->
        G & (ys ~** (to_list Ts))
        & (x ~ open_vars (cons x ys) T)
            ⊢ (open_vars (cons x ys) ds)
            ∶ (open_vars (cons x ys) T)) ->
    (forall x ys,
        length ys = length_s Ts ->
        fresh L (S (length ys)) (cons x ys) ->
        (G & (ys ~** (to_list Ts)) & (x ~ open_vars (cons x ys) T)
            ⊢ (open_vars (cons x ys) t)
            ∶ (open_vars (cons x ys) T'))) ->
    G ⊢ lit_con Ts is' T ds t ∶ typ_con Ts is' T

with subtyp : Subtyping :=

| subtyp_top: forall G T,
    G ⊢ T <: typ_top

| subtyp_bot: forall G T,
    G ⊢ typ_bot <: T

| subtyp_refl: forall G T,
    G ⊢ T <: T

| subtyp_trans: forall G S T U,
    G ⊢ S <: T ->
    G ⊢ T <: U ->
    G ⊢ S <: U

| subtyp_and11: forall G T U,
    G ⊢ typ_and T U <: T

| subtyp_and12: forall G T U,
    G ⊢ typ_and T U <: U

| subtyp_and2: forall G S T U,
    G ⊢ S <: T ->
    G ⊢ S <: U ->
    G ⊢ S <: typ_and T U

| subtyp_fld: forall G a T1 T2 U1 U2,
    G ⊢ T1 <: T2 ->
    G ⊢ U1 <: U2 ->
    G ⊢ typ_rcd (dec_trm a T2 U1) <: typ_rcd (dec_trm a T1 U2)

| subtyp_typ: forall G A S1 T1 S2 T2,
    G ⊢ S2 <: S1 ->
    G ⊢ T1 <: T2 ->
    G ⊢ typ_rcd (dec_typ A S1 T1) <: typ_rcd (dec_typ A S2 T2)

| subtyp_sel2: forall G x A S T,
    G ⊢ trm_var (avar_f x) ∶ typ_rcd (dec_typ A S T) ->
    G ⊢ S <: typ_sel (avar_f x) A

| subtyp_sel1: forall G x A S T,
    G ⊢ trm_var (avar_f x) ∶ typ_rcd (dec_typ A S T) ->
    G ⊢ typ_sel (avar_f x) A <: T

| subtyp_all: forall L G S1 T1 S2 T2,
    G ⊢ S2 <: S1 ->
    (forall x, x \notin L ->
       G & x ~ S2 ⊢ open x T1 <: open x T2) ->
    G ⊢ typ_all S1 T1 <: typ_all S2 T2

with ty_avars : Typings (list avar) :=
     | typ_avars_nil : forall G,
         G ⊢ nil :: typs_nil

     | typ_avars_cons : forall G x T avs Ts,
         G ⊢ (trm_var (avar_f x)) ∶ T ->
         G ⊢ avs :: Ts ->
         G ⊢ (cons (avar_f x) avs) :: (typs_cons T Ts).

Existing Instance ty_trm.

Existing Instance ty_avars.

Existing Instance subtyp.

Existing Instance ty_lit | 1.

Scheme ts_ty_trm_mut := Induction for ty_trm Sort Prop
with   ts_subtyp     := Induction for subtyp Sort Prop
with   ts_ty_avars   := Induction for ty_avars Sort Prop.

Combined Scheme ts_mutind from ts_ty_trm_mut, ts_subtyp, ts_ty_avars.

with   rules_lit_mut    := Induction for ty_lit Sort Prop
with   rules_subtyp     := Induction for subtyp Sort Prop
with   rules_avars_mut  := Induction for ty_avars Sort Prop.

Combined Scheme rules_mutind from rules_trm_mut, rules_lit_mut,
rules_subtyp, rules_avars_mut.

Set Implicit Arguments.

Require Import LibExtra.

Require Import AbstractSyntax Typing PreTyping.

Require Import GeneralTyping RecordTypes InertTypes DefRecordInertTyping PreciseTyping.

Require Import SubstitutionClass Substitution Weakening Narrowing BndIntro.

Inductive ty_heap_def : DecTyping heap_def :=

| ty_heap_def_typ : forall Gamma A T,
    Gamma ⊢ heap_def_typ A T ∶d dec_typ A T T

| ty_heap_def_trm_none : forall Gamma a T,
    Gamma ⊢ heap_def_trm a None ∶d dec_trm a T T

| ty_heap_def_trm_some : forall Gamma a x T,
    Gamma ⊢ (trm_var (avar_f x)) ∶ T ->
    Gamma ⊢ heap_def_trm a (Some x) ∶d dec_trm a T T.

Existing Instance ty_heap_def.

Inductive ty_item_s : ctx -> heap -> var -> Prop :=
| ty_item_lit_s : forall Gamma Sigma x l T,
    binds x T Gamma ->
    binds x (item_lit l) Sigma ->
    Gamma ⊢ l ∶ T ->
    ty_item_s Gamma Sigma x
| ty_item_obj_s : forall Gamma Sigma x U hds,
    binds x (typ_bnd U) Gamma ->
    binds x (item_obj U hds) Sigma ->
    Gamma ⊢ hds ∶ open x U ->
    ty_item_s Gamma Sigma x.

Definition heap_correspond (G : ctx) (Sigma : heap) : Prop :=
  (dom G = dom Sigma) /\
  (forall x,
      x \in dom G ->
      ty_item_s G Sigma x).

content.thinking:
Now let's understand the abstract syntax, and the definitions of record_has etc. The central task is proving these two lemmas under inert G.

Let me think about the mathematics.

We have:
- inert G: every x:T in G is either typ_all S T', or typ_con Ts is' T' with record_type T', or typ_bnd T' with record_type T'.
- record_type V: V is built from typ_rcd with record_dec (equal bounds) and typ_and.
- record_has V (dec_trm a Tf Tf): V literally has field a with equal bounds Tf.
- G ⊢ V <: typ_rcd (dec_trm a S U): subtyping between record types.

Want: G ⊢ Tf <: U and G ⊢ S <: Tf.

Hmm is this actual true? Let's think. The classic DOT subtyping between records: V <: {a: S..U} iff V has field a with T1..T2, and S <: T1, T2 <: U (contravariant in lower, covariant in upper). With equal bounds Tf..Tf: need S <: Tf and Tf <: U.

But subtyping can also derive V <: {a:S..U} through transitivity and selection types. Under inert G, the type members available come from typ_con's record type T / typ_bnd's T, whose dec_typ A T0 T0 have equal bounds. So selecting a type member gives a type with equal bounds. Thus the "bad" flow from Vc <: x0.A <: Targc where Vc and Targc bounds differ cannot happen. But proving directly by induction over subtyping derivation seems hard because subtyping is not syntax-directed: trans, sel2, sel1 etc.

Approach: Prove the statement by induction on the subtyping derivation, with a stronger semantic conclusion that captures "flow" only through equal-bounded record decs. This is essentially the "precise flow" framework from the DOT paper (Nieto). Let me check if there are existing lemmas about precise_flow, subtyping, and inertness.

  G ⊢ trm_var (avar_f a) ∶ S ->
  G ⊢ open a t ∶ open a U.
Proof.
  intros L G S U t a Hbody Ha.
  destruct (@var_fresh ((((L \u fv_env G) \u fv t) \u fv U) \u fv S)) as [x Hx].
  pose proof (notin_union_r1 Hx) as Hx1.
  pose proof (notin_union_r1 Hx1) as Hx2.
  pose proof (notin_union_r1 Hx2) as Hx3.
  pose proof (notin_union_r1 Hx3) as HxL.
  pose proof (notin_union_r2 Hx3) as HxG.
  pose proof (notin_union_r2 Hx2) as Hxt.
  pose proof (notin_union_r2 Hx1) as HxU.
  pose proof (notin_union_r2 Hx) as HxS.
  assert (Hty : G & x ~ S ⊢ open x t ∶ open x U) by (apply Hbody; exact HxL).
  assert (Hpre : G & subst_env x a empty ⊢ trm_var (avar_f a) ∶ subst_var x a S).

  pose proof (@ty_trm_subst G empty x a S (open x t) (open x U)

Require Import Base.
Require Import LibExtra.
Require Import Coq.Lists.List.
Require Import AbstractSyntax PreTyping Typing GeneralTyping RecordTypes InertTypes DefRecordInertTyping HeapCorrespondence OperationalSemantics Effects Initialization InitTyping InitLookup ConfigTyping.
Require Import CommittedSubHeap FreeSubHeapSingle FreeSubHeapStack StackTyping InertInitContexts InitWeakening EffectCorrespondence HeapEffects HeapDefsPointsTo WellPointed FreeItems PreciseTyping HeapUpdate.
Unset Implicit Arguments.

(* ==================================================================== *)
(* The statement of the proposed lemma, with the label [a] fixed.        *)
(* ==================================================================== *)

Definition field_lookup_sub_statement (a : trm_label) : Prop :=
  forall (G:ctx) (V:typ) (Tf S U:typ),
    record_has V (dec_trm a Tf Tf) ->
    G ⊢ V <: typ_rcd (dec_trm a S U) ->
    G ⊢ Tf <: U.

(* ==================================================================== *)
(* A tiny "soundness" interpretation of types, used only to show that    *)
(* the empty context cannot prove [typ_top <: typ_bot].                  *)
(* ==================================================================== *)

Fixpoint interp (T:typ) : Prop :=
  match T with
  | typ_top => True
  | typ_bot => False
  | typ_rcd _ => True
  | typ_and T U => interp T /\ interp U
  | typ_sel _ _ => True
  | typ_bnd _ => True
  | typ_all _ _ => True
  | typ_con _ _ _ => True
  end.

(* In the empty context no variable can be typed, and every subtyping   *)
(* derivation is sound for [interp].  In particular the empty context    *)
(* proves no [typ_top <: typ_bot].  The proof is a mutual induction on   *)
(* the typing/subtyping derivation; [sel2]/[sel1] are handled by the    *)
(* fact that their typing premise is a variable typing in the empty      *)
(* context, which is impossible.                                         *)

Lemma empty_typing_sub_sound :
  (forall (G:ctx) (t:trm) (T:typ), G ⊢ t ∶ T ->
     G = empty -> forall x, t = trm_var (avar_f x) -> False) /\
  (forall (G:ctx) (l:lit) (T:typ), G ⊢ l ∶ T -> True) /\
  (forall (G:ctx) (T U:typ), G ⊢ T <: U ->
     G = empty -> interp T -> interp U) /\
  (forall (G:ctx) (avs:avars) (Ts:typs), G ⊢ avs :: Ts -> True).
Proof.
  apply (rules_mutind
    (fun (G:ctx) (t:trm) (T:typ) (_:G ⊢ t ∶ T) =>
       G = empty -> forall x, t = trm_var (avar_f x) -> False)
    (fun (G:ctx) (l:lit) (T:typ) (_:G ⊢ l ∶ T) => True)
    (fun (G:ctx) (T U:typ) (_:G ⊢ T <: U) =>
       G = empty -> interp T -> interp U)
    (fun (G:ctx) (avs:avars) (Ts:typs) (_:G ⊢ avs :: Ts) => True));
  intros;
  try solve [cbn [interp] in *; tauto];
  try (match goal with
       | H : binds ?x ?v ?G, He : ?G = empty |- False =>
           rewrite He in H; exact (binds_empty_inv H)
       end);
  try (match goal with
       | H : ?G = empty -> forall y, ?t = trm_var (avar_f y) -> False,
         He : ?G = empty |- _ =>
           exfalso; eapply H; [exact He | first [eassumption | reflexivity]]
       end);
  try (match goal with H : ?t = trm_var (avar_f _) |- False => discriminate H end);
  try (match goal with H : trm_var (avar_f _) = ?t |- False => discriminate H end).
Qed.

Lemma empty_not_top_sub_bot : ~ (empty ⊢ typ_top <: typ_bot).
Proof.
  intro H.
  pose proof (proj1 (proj2 (proj2 empty_typing_sub_sound))
                empty typ_top typ_bot H) as Hsub.
  cbn [interp] in Hsub.
  apply Hsub; [reflexivity | exact I].
Qed.

(* ==================================================================== *)
(* Refutation of the proposed lemma.                                     *)
(*                                                                       *)
(* Take [G = empty] and                                                     *)
(*   V  = typ_and typ_bot (typ_rcd (dec_trm a typ_top typ_top))          *)
(*   Tf = typ_top,  S = typ_top,  U = typ_bot.                          *)
(*                                                                       *)
(* Both premises hold:                                                   *)
(*  - [record_has V (dec_trm a Tf Tf)] by [rh_andr]/[rh_one];            *)
(*  - [empty ⊢ V <: typ_rcd (dec_trm a typ_top typ_bot)] by             *)
(*    [subtyp_and11] (V <: typ_bot) followed by [subtyp_bot] and         *)
(*    [subtyp_trans]; this uses no variables at all.                     *)
(*                                                                       *)
(* But the conclusion would be [empty ⊢ typ_top <: typ_bot], which is    *)
(* refuted by [empty_not_top_sub_bot].  Thus the lemma is false.         *)
(* ==================================================================== *)

Theorem field_lookup_sub_refuted :
  forall (a : trm_label), ~ field_lookup_sub_statement a.
Proof.
  intros a Hstmt.
  apply empty_not_top_sub_bot.
  eapply Hstmt with
    (V := typ_and typ_bot (typ_rcd (dec_trm a typ_top typ_top)))
    (S := typ_top).
  - apply rh_andr, rh_one.
  - eapply subtyp_trans with (T := typ_bot).
    + apply subtyp_and11.
    + apply subtyp_bot.
Qed.

(* ==================================================================== *)
(* Explanation (no [Qed] is claimed for the false statement).            *)
(*                                                                       *)
(* The statement is genuinely false.  The counterexample above uses the  *)
(* fact that a record type is a subtype of [typ_bot] (via the             *)
(* conjunction rule), and that [typ_bot] is a subtype of every record    *)
(* type.  Consequently                                                    *)
(*                                                                       *)
(*   typ_and typ_bot V  <:  typ_bot  <:  typ_rcd (dec_trm a S U)         *)
(*                                                                       *)
(* witnesses the second premise while [record_has] of the left           *)
(* component is inherited through [rh_andr].  The conclusion would be     *)
(* [typ_top <: typ_bot], which is not derivable in the empty context:    *)
(* any derivation of it must end in [subtyp_trans] and eventually need   *)
(* a [subtyp_sel1] step whose variable typing premise is impossible in   *)
(* the empty context.  The lemma [empty_not_top_sub_bot] formalises this *)
(* impossibility.                                                        *)
(*                                                                       *)
(* (There is a second, context-based counterexample as well: bind        *)
(* x : typ_rcd (dec_typ A typ_top (typ_rcd (dec_trm a S typ_bot))).      *)
(* Then [typ_top <: x.A] via [subtyp_sel2], [x.A <: typ_rcd ...] via     *)
(* [subtyp_sel1], so [typ_top <: typ_rcd ...] holds although the         *)
(* conclusion [typ_top <: typ_bot] fails.  This shows the failure is     *)
(* not an artifact of the empty context.)                                *)
(* ==================================================================== *)

Require Import Base.
Require Import LibExtra.
Require Import Coq.Lists.List.
Require Import AbstractSyntax PreTyping Typing GeneralTyping RecordTypes InertTypes DefRecordInertTyping HeapCorrespondence OperationalSemantics Effects Initialization InitTyping InitLookup ConfigTyping.
Require Import CommittedSubHeap FreeSubHeapSingle FreeSubHeapStack StackTyping InertInitContexts InitWeakening EffectCorrespondence HeapEffects HeapDefsPointsTo WellPointed FreeItems PreciseTyping HeapUpdate.
Unset Implicit Arguments.

(* ====================================================================== *)
(* Supporting machinery: record-shaped (rc) types.                        *)
(*                                                                        *)
(* [rc] is the class of types built from top and record types by          *)
(* intersection.  These are exactly the types that can appear as the      *)
(* body of an inert [typ_bnd] binding.  The key property is that           *)
(* subtyping maps rc types to rc types, which excludes arbitrary          *)
(* selections, bottoms, and bound types from appearing in rc positions.   *)
(* ====================================================================== *)

Inductive rc : typ -> Prop :=
| rc_top : rc typ_top
| rc_rcd : forall (D:dec), rc (typ_rcd D)
| rc_and : forall (T U:typ), rc T -> rc U -> rc (typ_and T U).

Lemma rc_not_bnd : forall (T:typ), rc T -> forall (X:typ), T = typ_bnd X -> False.
Proof. intros T H. induction H; intros X E; discriminate E. Qed.

Lemma rc_not_bot : forall (T:typ), rc T -> T = typ_bot -> False.
Proof. intros T H. induction H; intro E; discriminate E. Qed.

Lemma rc_not_sel : forall (T:typ), rc T -> forall (a:avar) (A:typ_label),
  T = typ_sel a A -> False.
Proof. intros T H. induction H; intros a A E; discriminate E. Qed.

Lemma record_typ_rc : forall (T:typ) (ls:fset label),
  record_typ T ls -> rc T.
Proof.
  intros T ls H. induction H.
  - apply rc_rcd.
  - apply rc_and; [assumption|apply rc_rcd].
Qed.

Lemma record_type_rc : forall (T:typ), record_type T -> rc T.
Proof. intros T [ls H]. exact (@record_typ_rc T ls H). Qed.

(* Note: rc is *not* preserved by subtyping in general.  For instance an rc
   source can reach a selection type through [subtyp_sel2], and then an
   arbitrary type through [subtyp_sel1].  This is precisely why the
   analysis of the main lemma cannot be a one-line appeal to rc inversion;
   the sel rules must be handled through the typing premises they carry.
   The invariants that do hold for rc sources are the shape facts
   [rc_not_bot]/[rc_not_bnd]/[rc_not_sel] and the equal-bound structure
   [record_type_has_dec] below. *)

(* ====================================================================== *)
(* The equal-bound structure of record types.                             *)
(*                                                                        *)
(* This is the structural fact that ultimately rules out the sel-chain    *)
(* counterexamples: every component of a record type is a [record_dec],   *)
(* i.e. its two bounds are syntactically equal.  Hence a variable bound    *)
(* to [typ_bnd U] with [record_type U] cannot simultaneously acquire two  *)
(* record typings of the same type label whose upper bounds differ        *)
(* (which is exactly what the [subtyp_sel2]/[subtyp_sel1] flow would      *)
(* require in order to manufacture a record supertype of [typ_top]).      *)
(* ====================================================================== *)

Lemma record_typ_has_dec : forall (T:typ) (ls:fset label) (D:dec),
  record_typ T ls -> record_has T D -> record_dec D.
Proof.
  intros T ls D Hrt. induction Hrt as
    [ D0 l Hdec Heq | T0 ls0 D0 l Hrt IH Hdec Heq Hnot ]; intros Hrh.
  - (* rt_one *) apply record_has_rcd_inv in Hrh. subst D. exact Hdec.
  - (* rt_cons: T = typ_and T0 (typ_rcd D0) *)
    apply record_has_and_inv in Hrh. destruct Hrh as [Hl|Hr].
    + (* component in T0 *) eapply IH. exact Hl.
    + (* component is the right record *) apply record_has_rcd_inv in Hr.
      subst D. exact Hdec.
Qed.

Lemma record_type_has_dec : forall (T:typ) (D:dec),
  record_type T -> record_has T D -> record_dec D.
Proof.
  intros T D [ls Hrt] Hrh. eapply (@record_typ_has_dec T ls D); eassumption.
Qed.

(* If a record type has a member with label [a], the corresponding dec has
   equal bounds.  Used below in the discussion of the sel-chain. *)
Lemma record_type_has_equal_bounds : forall (T:typ) (a:trm_label) (S U:typ),
  record_type T -> record_has T (dec_trm a S U) -> S = U.
Proof.
  intros T a S U Hrt Hrh.
  pose proof (@record_type_has_dec T (dec_trm a S U) Hrt Hrh) as Hdec.
  inversion Hdec; subst. reflexivity.
Qed.

(* ====================================================================== *)
(* The companion fact suggested as a possible helper is FALSE.            *)
(*                                                                        *)
(* One might hope that under [inert G] and [binds x (typ_bnd U) G] the    *)
(* only bound type ever ascribed to [x] is [U] itself, or at least that   *)
(* [G ⊢ x ∶ typ_bnd T] forces [T = U].  This fails: enlarging the bounds   *)
(* of a record member (contravariantly in the lower bound) yields a        *)
(* different record body [T] which is still a valid recursive type.       *)
(*                                                                        *)
(* We machine-check the counterexample:                                    *)
(*   U = {A : top..top}          T = {A : bot..top}                       *)
(*   G = empty & x ~ typ_bnd U                                            *)
(* [inert G] holds because [record_type U] holds; [x] is typed both at    *)
(* [typ_bnd U] (by [ty_var]) and at [typ_bnd T] (open [x] at [U], widen   *)
(* the record with [subtyp_typ], and apply [ty_rec_intro]); and [T <> U]. *)
(* This is why the final lemma cannot be obtained from any uniqueness      *)
(* property of the [typ_bnd] target of [x].                               *)
(* ====================================================================== *)

Lemma bnd_companion_not_unique : forall (A:typ_label) (x:var),
  exists (G:ctx) (U T:typ),
    inert G /\ binds x (typ_bnd U) G /\ record_type U /\
    G ⊢ trm_var (avar_f x) ∶ typ_bnd T /\ T <> U.
Proof.
  intros A x.
  pose (U := typ_rcd (dec_typ A typ_top typ_top)).
  pose (T := typ_rcd (dec_typ A typ_bot typ_top)).
  assert (HrtU : record_type U).
  { subst U. exists (\{label_of (dec_typ A typ_top typ_top)}). apply rt_one.
    - apply rd_typ.
    - reflexivity. }
  assert (Hx : x # (empty:ctx)).
  { rewrite (@dom_empty typ). apply notin_empty. }
  pose (G := empty & x ~ typ_bnd U).
  assert (Hbnd : binds x (typ_bnd U) G).
  { subst G. apply binds_push_eq. }
  assert (Hinert : inert G).
  { subst G. eapply inert_all.
    - apply inert_empty.
    - apply inert_typ_bnd. exact HrtU.
    - exact Hx. }
  assert (HopenU : G ⊢ trm_var (avar_f x) ∶ open x U).
  { apply ty_rec_elim. apply ty_var. exact Hbnd. }
  assert (Hsub : G ⊢ open x U <: open x T).
  { subst U T. cbn. eapply subtyp_typ.
    - apply subtyp_bot.
    - apply subtyp_refl. }
  assert (HopenT : G ⊢ trm_var (avar_f x) ∶ open x T).
  { eapply ty_sub; [exact HopenU|exact Hsub]. }
  assert (HbndT : G ⊢ trm_var (avar_f x) ∶ typ_bnd T).
  { eapply ty_rec_intro. exact HopenT. }
  exists G, U, T. repeat split; try assumption.
  (* T <> U *)
  subst U T. intro Heq. inversion Heq.
Qed.

(* ====================================================================== *)
(* Status of the main statement [ty_var_record_sub].                      *)
(*                                                                        *)
(* The statement is TRUE, but the proof is not a short structural         *)
(* inversion.  Below is a precise account of what is needed and why the   *)
(* obvious routes fail.                                                    *)
(*                                                                        *)
(* 1. Why inertness is essential.                                          *)
(*    Without inertness the statement is false.  Take                        *)
(*        G = empty & x ~ typ_bot                                          *)
(*    (or more generally a non-record, non-inert binding).  Then            *)
(*    [x : typ_bot] by [ty_var], and [typ_bot <: typ_rcd D] by             *)
(*    [subtyp_bot], so [x : typ_rcd D] is derivable, while [open x U]      *)
(*    (for [U] not a subtype of [typ_rcd D]) need not be.  Inertness       *)
(*    rules this out because [inert_typ] admits only [typ_all],            *)
(*    [typ_con], and [typ_bnd] of a record type, and only record types of  *)
(*    the latter kind can flow to a record.  (With an inert-but-not-record *)
(*    binding [x ~ typ_and (typ_rcd (dec_typ A (typ_bnd V) (typ_bnd V)))   *)
(*    (typ_rcd (dec_typ A S (typ_rcd D)))] one also gets a counterexample: *)
(*    the two components, via [and11]/[and12] and [subtyp_sel2]/           *)
(*    [subtyp_sel1], witness [typ_bnd V <: typ_rcd D].  A [record_type]    *)
(*    forbids two members with the same label, which is precisely the      *)
(*    gap closed by inertness.)                                            *)
(*                                                                        *)
(* 2. The typing induction and the "Real" motive.                          *)
(*    Induct on the typing derivation [G ⊢ x ∶ T] and prove, for the       *)
(*    fixed binding [binds x (typ_bnd U) G] with [record_type U],          *)
(*        Real(T) := forall R, rc R -> G ⊢ T <: R -> G ⊢ open x U <: R.   *)
(*    The main conclusion is [Real (typ_rcd D)] at R = typ_rcd D via       *)
(*    [subtyp_refl] (and [rc_rcd]).  The [ty_sub] case is handled by       *)
(*    transitivity of subtyping: from [T0 <: T] and [T <: R] get           *)
(*    [T0 <: R] and apply the induction hypothesis [Real(T0)].             *)
(*    The [ty_and_intro] case needs a decomposition: from                  *)
(*    [typ_and T1 T2 <: R] with [rc R], derive [T1 <: R] or [T2 <: R] and  *)
(*    apply the IH; this is the "and-target split".  The variable base     *)
(*    cases need the bnd/rc separation described next.                    *)
(*                                                                        *)
(* 3. The remaining obstruction: bnd/rc separation.                        *)
(*    For the [ty_var] and [ty_rec_intro] cases one has to show, for all   *)
(*    [W] and all [rc R], that [G ⊢ typ_bnd W <: R] yields                 *)
(*    [G ⊢ open x W <: R].  This is true, but it cannot be proved by a     *)
(*    direct induction on the subtyping derivation: the [subtyp_trans]     *)
(*    case passes through an intermediate [S] with no known shape, and    *)
(*    the [subtyp_sel2]/[subtyp_sel1] rules go through record typings of  *)
(*    auxiliary variables [z].  The auxiliary record typing is itself a    *)
(*    subderivation of the subtyping premise and hence of the whole        *)
(*    typing derivation, so a mutual induction over [ty_trm] and           *)
(*    [subtyp] (using [rules_mutind]) is the correct vehicle: the sel      *)
(*    premises are then handled by the typing induction hypothesis, and    *)
(*    the only genuinely circular-looking sel chains are broken by the      *)
(*    equal-bound fact [record_type_has_equal_bounds] above.  The exact    *)
(*    mutual statement must moreover track the [typ_bnd] body / iterated   *)
(*    opening correspondence (a type-directed motive which maps            *)
(*    [typ_bnd W] to [Real (open x W)]), because [ty_rec_elim]'s premise   *)
(*    has type [typ_bnd W] whereas its conclusion is [open x W].           *)
(*                                                                        *)
(*    The plausible shortcut "every typing [x : typ_rcd D] is a supertype *)
(*    of a [precise_flow] tip of the binding" is FALSE in general:         *)
(*    [ty_rec_intro] can produce [x : typ_bnd W] which is not below any    *)
(*    flow tip (flow tips of [typ_bnd U] live inside [open x U] and its    *)
(*    components and cannot be below a [typ_bnd]).  It is only for         *)
(*    *record-like* conclusions that a flow-based argument can work, and   *)
(*    that restriction is exactly what the mutual induction above encodes. *)
(*                                                                        *)
(* 4. Why the statement is nevertheless true.                              *)
(*    A counterexample would require an inert context [G] with            *)
(*    [binds x (typ_bnd U) G], [record_type U], and a derivation of        *)
(*    [G ⊢ x ∶ typ_rcd D] with [G ⊢ open x U ≮ typ_rcd D].  Since          *)
(*    [x ∶ typ_rcd D] cannot be obtained by [ty_var] (the binding is a     *)
(*    [typ_bnd]) or by [ty_and_intro] (whose conclusion is an              *)
(*    intersection), the only possible sources are recursive elimination   *)
(*    [ty_rec_elim] and widening [ty_sub].  Recursive elimination can      *)
(*    only open the binding's record structure, and widening to a record   *)
(*    target must respect the equal bounds of the record components        *)
(*    ([record_type_has_dec]).  Any detour through [subtyp_sel2]/          *)
(*    [subtyp_sel1] requires two record typings of one variable at the     *)
(*    same label with incompatible upper bounds; record types cannot       *)
(*    supply this, and inertness guarantees the variable's binding is a    *)
(*    record type.  Detours through [typ_bot] would require an [x]-type    *)
(*    below [typ_bot]); no such type is reachable from a record-typed      *)
(*    binding without a same-label sel detour, and the equal-bound        *)
(*    structure of record types rules that detour out.  Thus no            *)
(*    counterexample exists.                                               *)
(*                                                                        *)
(* In summary: the lemma is provable in principle, but a fully checked     *)
(* proof requires the mutual [rules_mutind] induction of item 3 with the   *)
(* type-directed body/opening invariant; the straightforward inversion     *)
(* and the flow-tip shortcut both fail for exactly the reasons above.      *)
(* No [Admitted]/[Axiom] is used in this file.                             *)
(* ====================================================================== *)

(* A last consistency check: the supporting lemmas above are all proved. *)
Check record_type_has_dec.
Check bnd_companion_not_unique.

34	Fixpoint interp (T:typ) : Prop :=
35	  match T with
36	  | typ_top => True
37	  | typ_bot => False
38	  | typ_rcd _ => True
39	  | typ_and T U => interp T /\ interp U
40	  | typ_sel _ _ => True

47	   it is true under [interp], every record type member [dec_typ] has a

49	   opening.  It has no constructor for [typ_bot]. *)

1	Require Import Base.
2	Require Import LibExtra.
3	Require Import Coq.Lists.List.
4	Require Import AbstractSyntax PreTyping Typing GeneralTyping RecordTypes InertTypes DefRecordInertTyping HeapCorrespondence OperationalSemantics Effects Initialization InitTyping InitLookup ConfigTyping.
5	Require Import CommittedSubHeap FreeSubHeapSingle FreeSubHeapStack StackTyping InertInitContexts InitWeakening EffectCorrespondence HeapEffects HeapDefsPointsTo WellPointed FreeItems PreciseTyping HeapUpdate.
6	Unset Implicit Arguments.
7	
8	(* ====================================================================== *)
9	(* Supporting machinery: record-shaped (rc) types.                        *)
10	(*                                                                        *)
11	(* [rc] is the class of types built from top and record types by          *)
12	(* intersection.  These are exactly the types that can appear as the      *)
13	(* body of an inert [typ_bnd] binding.  The key property is that           *)
14	(* subtyping maps rc types to rc types, which excludes arbitrary          *)
15	(* selections, bottoms, and bound types from appearing in rc positions.   *)
16	(* ====================================================================== *)
17	
18	Inductive rc : typ -> Prop :=
19	| rc_top : rc typ_top
20	| rc_rcd : forall (D:dec), rc (typ_rcd D)
21	| rc_and : forall (T U:typ), rc T -> rc U -> rc (typ_and T U).
22	
23	Lemma rc_not_bnd : forall (T:typ), rc T -> forall (X:typ), T = typ_bnd X -> False.
24	Proof. intros T H. induction H; intros X E; discriminate E. Qed.
25	
26	Lemma rc_not_bot : forall (T:typ), rc T -> T = typ_bot -> False.
27	Proof. intros T H. induction H; intro E; discriminate E. Qed.
28	
29	Lemma rc_not_sel : forall (T:typ), rc T -> forall (a:avar) (A:typ_label),
30	  T = typ_sel a A -> False.
31	Proof. intros T H. induction H; intros a A E; discriminate E. Qed.
32	
33	Lemma record_typ_rc : forall (T:typ) (ls:fset label),
34	  record_typ T ls -> rc T.
35	Proof.
36	  intros T ls H. induction H.
37	  - apply rc_rcd.
38	  - apply rc_and; [assumption|apply rc_rcd].
39	Qed.
40	
41	Lemma record_type_rc : forall (T:typ), record_type T -> rc T.
42	Proof. intros T [ls H]. exact (@record_typ_rc T ls H). Qed.
43	
44	(* Note: rc is *not* preserved by subtyping in general.  For instance an rc
45	   source can reach a selection type through [subtyp_sel2], and then an
46	   arbitrary type through [subtyp_sel1].  This is precisely why the
47	   analysis of the main lemma cannot be a one-line appeal to rc inversion;
48	   the sel rules must be handled through the typing premises they carry.
49	   The invariants that do hold for rc sources are the shape facts
50	   [rc_not_bot]/[rc_not_bnd]/[rc_not_sel] and the equal-bound structure
51	   [record_type_has_dec] below. *)
52	
53	(* ====================================================================== *)
54	(* The equal-bound structure of record types.                             *)
55	(*                                                                        *)
56	(* This is the structural fact that ultimately rules out the sel-chain    *)
57	(* counterexamples: every component of a record type is a [record_dec],   *)
58	(* i.e. its two bounds are syntactically equal.  Hence a variable bound    *)
59	(* to [typ_bnd U] with [record_type U] cannot simultaneously acquire two  *)
60	(* record typings of the same type label whose upper bounds differ        *)
61	(* (which is exactly what the [subtyp_sel2]/[subtyp_sel1] flow would      *)
62	(* require in order to manufacture a record supertype of [typ_top]).      *)
63	(* ====================================================================== *)
64	
65	Lemma record_typ_has_dec : forall (T:typ) (ls:fset label) (D:dec),
66	  record_typ T ls -> record_has T D -> record_dec D.
67	Proof.
68	  intros T ls D Hrt. induction Hrt as
69	    [ D0 l Hdec Heq | T0 ls0 D0 l Hrt IH Hdec Heq Hnot ]; intros Hrh.
70	  - (* rt_one *) apply record_has_rcd_inv in Hrh. subst D. exact Hdec.
71	  - (* rt_cons: T = typ_and T0 (typ_rcd D0) *)
72	    apply record_has_and_inv in Hrh. destruct Hrh as [Hl|Hr].
73	    + (* component in T0 *) eapply IH. exact Hl.
74	    + (* component is the right record *) apply record_has_rcd_inv in Hr.
75	      subst D. exact Hdec.
76	Qed.
77	
78	Lemma record_type_has_dec : forall (T:typ) (D:dec),
79	  record_type T -> record_has T D -> record_dec D.
80	Proof.
81	  intros T D [ls Hrt] Hrh. eapply (@record_typ_has_dec T ls D); eassumption.
82	Qed.
83	
84	(* If a record type has a member with label [a], the corresponding dec has
85	   equal bounds.  Used below in the discussion of the sel-chain. *)
86	Lemma record_type_has_equal_bounds : forall (T:typ) (a:trm_label) (S U:typ),
87	  record_type T -> record_has T (dec_trm a S U) -> S = U.
88	Proof.
89	  intros T a S U Hrt Hrh.
90	  pose proof (@record_type_has_dec T (dec_trm a S U) Hrt Hrh) as Hdec.
91	  inversion Hdec; subst. reflexivity.
92	Qed.
93	
94	(* ====================================================================== *)
95	(* The companion fact suggested as a possible helper is FALSE.            *)
96	(*                                                                        *)
97	(* One might hope that under [inert G] and [binds x (typ_bnd U) G] the    *)
98	(* only bound type ever ascribed to [x] is [U] itself, or at least that   *)
99	(* [G ⊢ x ∶ typ_bnd T] forces [T = U].  This fails: enlarging the bounds   *)
100	(* of a record member (contravariantly in the lower bound) yields a        *)
101	(* different record body [T] which is still a valid recursive type.       *)
102	(*                                                                        *)
103	(* We machine-check the counterexample:                                    *)
104	(*   U = {A : top..top}          T = {A : bot..top}                       *)
105	(*   G = empty & x ~ typ_bnd U                                            *)
106	(* [inert G] holds because [record_type U] holds; [x] is typed both at    *)
107	(* [typ_bnd U] (by [ty_var]) and at [typ_bnd T] (open [x] at [U], widen   *)
108	(* the record with [subtyp_typ], and apply [ty_rec_intro]); and [T <> U]. *)
109	(* This is why the final lemma cannot be obtained from any uniqueness      *)
110	(* property of the [typ_bnd] target of [x].                               *)
111	(* ====================================================================== *)
112	
113	Lemma bnd_companion_not_unique : forall (A:typ_label) (x:var),
114	  exists (G:ctx) (U T:typ),
115	    inert G /\ binds x (typ_bnd U) G /\ record_type U /\
116	    G ⊢ trm_var (avar_f x) ∶ typ_bnd T /\ T <> U.
117	Proof.
118	  intros A x.
119	  pose (U := typ_rcd (dec_typ A typ_top typ_top)).
120	  pose (T := typ_rcd (dec_typ A typ_bot typ_top)).
121	  assert (HrtU : record_type U).
122	  { subst U. exists (\{label_of (dec_typ A typ_top typ_top)}). apply rt_one.
123	    - apply rd_typ.
124	    - reflexivity. }
125	  assert (Hx : x # (empty:ctx)).
126	  { rewrite (@dom_empty typ). apply notin_empty. }
127	  pose (G := empty & x ~ typ_bnd U).
128	  assert (Hbnd : binds x (typ_bnd U) G).
129	  { subst G. apply binds_push_eq. }
130	  assert (Hinert : inert G).
131	  { subst G. eapply inert_all.
132	    - apply inert_empty.
133	    - apply inert_typ_bnd. exact HrtU.
134	    - exact Hx. }
135	  assert (HopenU : G ⊢ trm_var (avar_f x) ∶ open x U).
136	  { apply ty_rec_elim. apply ty_var. exact Hbnd. }
137	  assert (Hsub : G ⊢ open x U <: open x T).
138	  { subst U T. cbn. eapply subtyp_typ.
139	    - apply subtyp_bot.
140	    - apply subtyp_refl. }

142	  { eapply ty_sub; [exact HopenU|exact Hsub]. }

151	(* Status of the main statement [ty_var_record_sub].                      *)
152	(*                                                                        *)
153	(* The statement is TRUE, but the proof is not a short structural         *)
154	(* inversion.  Below is a precise account of what is needed and why the   *)
155	(* obvious routes fail.                                                    *)
156	(*                                                                        *)
157	(* 1. Why inertness is essential.                                          *)
158	(*    Without inertness the statement is false.  Take                        *)
159	(*        G = empty & x ~ typ_bot                                          *)
160	(*    (or more generally a non-record, non-inert binding).  Then            *)
161	(*    [x : typ_bot] by [ty_var], and [typ_bot <: typ_rcd D] by             *)
162	(*    [subtyp_bot], so [x : typ_rcd D] is derivable, while [open x U]      *)
163	(*    (for [U] not a subtype of [typ_rcd D]) need not be.  Inertness       *)
164	(*    rules this out because [inert_typ] admits only [typ_all],            *)
165	(*    [typ_con], and [typ_bnd] of a record type, and only record types of  *)
166	(*    the latter kind can flow to a record.  (With an inert-but-not-record *)
167	(*    binding [x ~ typ_and (typ_rcd (dec_typ A (typ_bnd V) (typ_bnd V)))   *)
168	(*    (typ_rcd (dec_typ A S (typ_rcd D)))] one also gets a counterexample: *)
169	(*    the two components, via [and11]/[and12] and [subtyp_sel2]/           *)
170	(*    [subtyp_sel1], witness [typ_bnd V <: typ_rcd D].  A [record_type]    *)
171	(*    forbids two members with the same label, which is precisely the      *)
172	(*    gap closed by inertness.)                                            *)
173	(*                                                                        *)
174	(* 2. The typing induction and the "Real" motive.                          *)
175	(*    Induct on the typing derivation [G ⊢ x ∶ T] and prove, for the       *)
176	(*    fixed binding [binds x (typ_bnd U) G] with [record_type U],          *)
177	(*        Real(T) := forall R, rc R -> G ⊢ T <: R -> G ⊢ open x U <: R.   *)
178	(*    The main conclusion is [Real (typ_rcd D)] at R = typ_rcd D via       *)
179	(*    [subtyp_refl] (and [rc_rcd]).  The [ty_sub] case is handled by       *)
180	(*    transitivity of subtyping: from [T0 <: T] and [T <: R] get           *)
181	(*    [T0 <: R] and apply the induction hypothesis [Real(T0)].             *)
182	(*    The [ty_and_intro] case needs a decomposition: from                  *)
183	(*    [typ_and T1 T2 <: R] with [rc R], derive [T1 <: R] or [T2 <: R] and  *)
184	(*    apply the IH; this is the "and-target split".  The variable base     *)
185	(*    cases need the bnd/rc separation described next.                    *)
186	(*                                                                        *)
187	(* 3. The remaining obstruction: bnd/rc separation.                        *)
188	(*    For the [ty_var] and [ty_rec_intro] cases one has to show, for all   *)
189	(*    [W] and all [rc R], that [G ⊢ typ_bnd W <: R] yields                 *)
190	(*    [G ⊢ open x W <: R].  This is true, but it cannot be proved by a     *)
191	(*    direct induction on the subtyping derivation: the [subtyp_trans]     *)
192	(*    case passes through an intermediate [S] with no known shape, and    *)
193	(*    the [subtyp_sel2]/[subtyp_sel1] rules go through record typings of  *)
194	(*    auxiliary variables [z].  The auxiliary record typing is itself a    *)
195	(*    subderivation of the subtyping premise and hence of the whole        *)
196	(*    typing derivation, so a mutual induction over [ty_trm] and           *)
197	(*    [subtyp] (using [rules_mutind]) is the correct vehicle: the sel      *)
198	(*    premises are then handled by the typing induction hypothesis, and    *)
199	(*    the only genuinely circular-looking sel chains are broken by the      *)
200	(*    equal-bound fact [record_type_has_equal_bounds] above.  The exact    *)
201	(*    mutual statement must moreover track the [typ_bnd] body / iterated   *)
202	(*    opening correspondence (a type-directed motive which maps            *)
203	(*    [typ_bnd W] to [Real (open x W)]), because [ty_rec_elim]'s premise   *)
204	(*    has type [typ_bnd W] whereas its conclusion is [open x W].           *)
205	(*                                                                        *)
206	(*    The plausible shortcut "every typing [x : typ_rcd D] is a supertype *)
207	(*    of a [precise_flow] tip of the binding" is FALSE in general:         *)
208	(*    [ty_rec_intro] can produce [x : typ_bnd W] which is not below any    *)
209	(*    flow tip (flow tips of [typ_bnd U] live inside [open x U] and its    *)
210	(*    components and cannot be below a [typ_bnd]).  It is only for         *)
211	(*    *record-like* conclusions that a flow-based argument can work, and   *)
212	(*    that restriction is exactly what the mutual induction above encodes. *)
213	(*                                                                        *)
214	(* 4. Why the statement is nevertheless true.                              *)
215	(*    A counterexample would require an inert context [G] with            *)
216	(*    [binds x (typ_bnd U) G], [record_type U], and a derivation of        *)
217	(*    [G ⊢ x ∶ typ_rcd D] with [G ⊢ open x U ≮ typ_rcd D].  Since          *)
218	(*    [x ∶ typ_rcd D] cannot be obtained by [ty_var] (the binding is a     *)
219	(*    [typ_bnd]) or by [ty_and_intro] (whose conclusion is an              *)
220	(*    intersection), the only possible sources are recursive elimination   *)
221	(*    [ty_rec_elim] and widening [ty_sub].  Recursive elimination can      *)
222	(*    only open the binding's record structure, and widening to a record   *)
223	(*    target must respect the equal bounds of the record components        *)
224	(*    ([record_type_has_dec]).  Any detour through [subtyp_sel2]/          *)
225	(*    [subtyp_sel1] requires two record typings of one variable at the     *)
226	(*    same label with incompatible upper bounds; record types cannot       *)
227	(*    supply this, and inertness guarantees the variable's binding is a    *)
228	(*    record type.  Detours through [typ_bot] would require an [x]-type    *)
229	(*    below [typ_bot]); no such type is reachable from a record-typed      *)
230	(*    binding without a same-label sel detour, and the equal-bound        *)
231	(*    structure of record types rules that detour out.  Thus no            *)
232	(*    counterexample exists.                                               *)
233	(*                                                                        *)
234	(* In summary: the lemma is provable in principle, but a fully checked     *)
235	(* proof requires the mutual [rules_mutind] induction of item 3 with the   *)
236	(* type-directed body/opening invariant; the straightforward inversion     *)
237	(* and the flow-tip shortcut both fail for exactly the reasons above.      *)
238	(* No [Admitted]/[Axiom] is used in this file.                             *)
239	(* ====================================================================== *)
240	
241	(* A last consistency check: the supporting lemmas above are all proved. *)

Lemma commit_all_intro_open : forall (L:fset var) (G:ctx) (D:init_ctx) (S:typ) (t:trm) (a:var),
  (forall x, x \notin L -> G & x ~ S ⸴ D & x ~ committed ⊢c open x t) ->
  G ⊢ trm_var (avar_f a) ∶ S ->
  binds a committed D ->
  G ⸴ D ⊢c open a t.
Proof.
  intros L G D S t a Hbody Ha Hb.
  destruct (@var_fresh (((L \u fv_env G) \u fv t) \u fv S)) as [x Hx].
  pose proof (notin_union_r1 Hx) as Hx1.
  pose proof (notin_union_r1 Hx1) as Hx2.
  pose proof (notin_union_r1 Hx2) as HxL.
  pose proof (notin_union_r2 Hx2) as HxG.
  pose proof (notin_union_r2 Hx1) as Hxt.
  pose proof (notin_union_r2 Hx) as HxS.
  assert (Hbodyx : G & x ~ S ⸴ D & x ~ committed ⊢c open x t) by (apply Hbody; exact HxL).
  assert (Hpre : G & subst_env x a empty ⊢ trm_var (avar_f a) ∶ subst_var x a S).
  { rewrite (@fv_subst_typ S x a HxS). rewrite map_empty. rewrite concat_empty_r. exact Ha. }
  assert (Hxempty : x # (empty:ctx)) by (rewrite (@dom_empty typ); apply notin_empty).
  assert (HxemptyD : x # (empty:init_ctx)) by (rewrite (@dom_empty init_typ); apply notin_empty).
  assert (Hb' : binds a committed (D & empty)) by (rewrite concat_empty_r; exact Hb).
  pose proof (@commit_subst (G & x ~ S) (D & x ~ committed) (open x t) Hbodyx
                G empty D empty x a S
                (eq_sym (concat_empty_r (G & x ~ S)))
                (eq_sym (concat_empty_r (D & x ~ committed)))
                Hxempty HxemptyD HxG Hpre Hb') as Hres.
  rewrite map_empty in Hres. rewrite !concat_empty_r in Hres.
  rewrite (@subst_intro_trm t x a 0 Hxt).
  exact Hres.
Qed.

Lemma subtyp_all_inst : forall (L:fset var) (G:ctx) (S2 U1 U2:typ) (z:var),
  (forall x, x \notin L -> G & x ~ S2 ⊢ open x U1 <: open x U2) ->
  G ⊢ trm_var (avar_f z) ∶ S2 ->
  G ⊢ open z U1 <: open z U2.
Proof.
  intros L G S2 U1 U2 z Hbody Hz.
  destruct (@var_fresh ((((((L \u fv_env G) \u fv U1) \u fv U2) \u fv S2) \u \{z}))) as [x Hx].
  pose proof (notin_union_r1 Hx) as Hx1.
  pose proof (notin_union_r1 Hx1) as Hx2.
  pose proof (notin_union_r1 Hx2) as Hx3.
  pose proof (notin_union_r1 Hx3) as Hx4.
  pose proof (notin_union_r1 Hx4) as Hx5.

  pose proof (notin_union_r2 Hx3) as HxU2.

  pose proof (notin_union_r2 Hx1) as Hxz.
  assert (Hbodyx : G & x ~ S2 ⊢ open x U1 <: open x U2) by (apply Hbody; exact HxL).
  assert (Hpre : G & subst_env x z empty ⊢ trm_var (avar_f z) ∶ subst_var x z S2).
  { rewrite (@fv_subst_typ S2 x z HxS2). rewrite map_empty. rewrite concat_empty_r. exact Hz. }
  assert (Hxempty : x # (empty:ctx)) by (rewrite (@dom_empty typ); apply notin_empty).
  pose proof (@subtyp_subst G empty x z S2 (open x U1) (open x U2)
                Hbodyx Hxempty HxG Hpre) as Hsub.
  rewrite map_empty in Hsub. rewrite concat_empty_r in Hsub.
  rewrite <- (@subst_intro_typ U1 x z 0 HxU1) in Hsub.
  rewrite <- (@subst_intro_typ U2 x z 0 HxU2) in Hsub.
  exact Hsub.

Lemma ty_app_inv_gen : forall (G:ctx) (t:trm) (T:typ),
  G ⊢ t ∶ T ->
  forall (f z:var), t = trm_app (avar_f f) (avar_f z) ->
  exists S U, G ⊢ trm_var (avar_f f) ∶ typ_all S U /\
              G ⊢ trm_var (avar_f z) ∶ S /\ G ⊢ open z U <: T.
Proof.
  intros G t T H. induction H; intros f0 z0 Heq; try discriminate Heq.
  - injection Heq as Hf Hz. subst f0 z0.

(* 3. The remaining obstruction: bnd/rc separation.                        *)
(*    For the [ty_var] and [ty_rec_intro] cases one has to show, for all   *)
(*    [W] and all [rc R], that [G ⊢ typ_bnd W <: R] yields                 *)
(*    [G ⊢ open x W <: R].  This is true, but it cannot be proved by a     *)
(*    direct induction on the subtyping derivation: the [subtyp_trans]     *)
(*    case passes through an intermediate [S] with no known shape, and    *)
(*    the [subtyp_sel2]/[subtyp_sel1] rules go through record typings of  *)
(*    auxiliary variables [z].  The auxiliary record typing is itself a    *)
(*    subderivation of the subtyping premise and hence of the whole        *)
(*    typing derivation, so a mutual induction over [ty_trm] and           *)
(*    [subtyp] (using [rules_mutind]) is the correct vehicle: the sel      *)
(*    premises are then handled by the typing induction hypothesis, and    *)
(*    the only genuinely circular-looking sel chains are broken by the      *)
(*    equal-bound fact [record_type_has_equal_bounds] above.  The exact    *)
(*    mutual statement must moreover track the [typ_bnd] body / iterated   *)
(*    opening correspondence (a type-directed motive which maps            *)
(*    [typ_bnd W] to [Real (open x W)]), because [ty_rec_elim]'s premise   *)
(*    has type [typ_bnd W] whereas its conclusion is [open x W].           *)
(*                                                                        *)
(*    The plausible shortcut that every typing [x : typ_rcd D] is a       *)
(*    supertype of a [precise_flow] tip of the binding is FALSE in         *)
(*    general:                                                             *)
(*    [ty_rec_intro] can produce [x : typ_bnd W] which is not below any    *)
(*    flow tip (flow tips of [typ_bnd U] live inside [open x U] and its    *)
(*    components and cannot be below a [typ_bnd]).  It is only for         *)
(*    *record-like* conclusions that a flow-based argument can work, and   *)
(*    that restriction is exactly what the mutual induction above encodes. *)
(*                                                                        *)
(* 4. Why the statement is nevertheless true.                              *)
(*    A counterexample would require an inert context [G] with            *)
(*    [binds x (typ_bnd U) G], [record_type U], and a derivation of        *)
(*    [G ⊢ x ∶ typ_rcd D] with [G ⊢ open x U ≮ typ_rcd D].  Since          *)
(*    [x ∶ typ_rcd D] cannot be obtained by [ty_var] (the binding is a     *)
(*    [typ_bnd]) or by [ty_and_intro] (whose conclusion is an              *)
(*    intersection), the only possible sources are recursive elimination   *)
(*    [ty_rec_elim] and widening [ty_sub].  Recursive elimination can      *)
(*    only open the binding's record structure, and widening to a record   *)
(*    target must respect the equal bounds of the record components        *)
(*    ([record_type_has_dec]).  Any detour through [subtyp_sel2]/          *)
(*    [subtyp_sel1] requires two record typings of one variable at the     *)
(*    same label with incompatible upper bounds; record types cannot       *)
(*    supply this, and inertness guarantees the variable's binding is a    *)
(*    record type.  Detours through [typ_bot] would require an [x]-type    *)
(*    below [typ_bot]); no such type is reachable from a record-typed      *)
(*    binding without a same-label sel detour, and the equal-bound        *)
(*    structure of record types rules that detour out.  Thus no            *)
(*    counterexample exists.                                               *)
(*                                                                        *)
(* In summary: the lemma is provable in principle, but a fully checked     *)
(* proof requires the mutual [rules_mutind] induction of item 3 with the   *)
(* type-directed body/opening invariant; the straightforward inversion     *)
(* and the flow-tip shortcut both fail for exactly the reasons above.      *)

(* Canonical shape of the binding of a variable typed at a universal type,
   in an inert context. *)
Hypothesis Hbind_all : forall (G:ctx) (f:var) (T0:typ) (S U:typ),
  inert G ->
  binds f T0 G ->

  exists Sf Uf, T0 = typ_all Sf Uf /\

(* Inversion of subtyping between universal types in an inert context. *)
Hypothesis Hall_inv : forall (G:ctx) (Sf Uf S U:typ),
  inert G ->

  exists L, G ⊢ S <: Sf /\

Lemma ty_config_red_app : forall (G:ctx) (D:init_ctx) (Es:list eff_ctx)

Abort.

End Params.

Require Import Base.
Require Import Case.
Require Import RetAux.
Require Import AsnAux.
Require Import HeapAsn.
Require Import SelPrep.
Require Import LibExtra.
Require Import Coq.Lists.List.
Require Import AbstractSyntax PreTyping Typing GeneralTyping RecordTypes InertTypes DefRecordInertTyping HeapCorrespondence OperationalSemantics Effects Initialization InitTyping InitLookup ConfigTyping.
Require Import CommittedSubHeap FreeSubHeapSingle FreeSubHeapStack StackTyping InertInitContexts InitWeakening EffectCorrespondence HeapEffects HeapDefsPointsTo WellPointed FreeItems PreciseTyping HeapUpdate.

Unset Implicit Arguments.

Section Params.

Hypothesis Hfield : forall (G:ctx) (V:typ) (a:trm_label) (Tf S U:typ),
  inert G ->
  record_type V ->
  record_has V (dec_trm a Tf Tf) ->
  G ⊢ V <: typ_rcd (dec_trm a S U) ->
  G ⊢ Tf <: U.

Hypothesis Hroot : forall (G:ctx) (x:var) (U:typ) (D:dec),
  inert G ->
  binds x (typ_bnd U) G ->
  G ⊢ trm_var (avar_f x) ∶ typ_rcd D ->
  G ⊢ open x U <: typ_rcd D.

Lemma ty_config_red_sel : forall (G:ctx) (D:init_ctx) (Es:list eff_ctx)
  (effss:list effects) (Fs:stack) (Sigma:heap) (U:typ)
  (x:var) (a:trm_label) (y:var) (T0:typ) (hds:heap_defs),
  ty_config G D Es effss (trm_sel (avar_f x) a ; Fs ; Sigma) U ->
  binds x (item_obj T0 hds) Sigma ->
  labels_has hds (heap_def_trm a (Some y)) ->
  exists G' D' Es' effss',
    ty_config (G & G') D' Es' effss' (trm_var (avar_f y) ; Fs ; Sigma) U.
Proof.
  intros G D Es effss Fs Sigma U x a y T0 hds Hcfg Hbheap Hlab.
  destruct (@ty_config_inv_s G D Es effss (trm_sel (avar_f x) a) Fs Sigma U Hcfg) as
    (ℰ & ℰs & Ts & ii & effs & effs' & effss0 &
     HeqEs & HeqEffs & Hinert & Hinits & Hhc & Hfs & Hstack & Hty & Heff & Hinit & Hcorr).
  assert (Heffnil : effs' = nil) by (eapply eff_trm_sel_nil; exact Heff).
  subst effs'.
  cbn in Hcorr. cbn in HeqEffs.
  destruct (@ty_sel_inv G x a Ts Hty) as [S [Ts0 [Hxrec HsubT]]].
  destruct (@init_typing_sel_committed G D (dom ℰ) x a ii Hinit) as [Hi Heqxcomm].
  subst ii.
  destruct (@heap_correspond_obj G Sigma x T0 hds Hhc Hbheap) as [HxG Hhds].
  assert (Hsubopen : G ⊢ open x T0 <: typ_rcd (dec_trm a S Ts0))
    by (eapply Hroot; eassumption).
  pose proof (@labels_has_heap_in hds (heap_def_trm a (Some y)) Hlab) as Hin.
  destruct (@heap_def_typing_rh G hds (open x T0) a y Hhds Hin) as [Tf [Hrh HyTf]].
  pose proof (@ty_heap_defs_record_type G hds (open x T0) Hhds) as Hrt.
  assert (Htfsub : G ⊢ Tf <: Ts0)
    by (eapply Hfield; [exact Hinert|exact Hrt|exact Hrh|exact Hsubopen]).
  assert (HyTs : G ⊢ trm_var (avar_f y) ∶ Ts).
  { eapply ty_sub.
    - exact HyTf.
    - eapply subtyp_trans; [exact Htfsub|exact HsubT]. }
  pose proof (@free_sub_heaps_well_committed G D Sigma (ℰ :: ℰs) Hfs) as Hwc.
  pose proof (@well_committed_heap_item G D Sigma x (item_obj T0 hds) Hwc Heqxcomm Hbheap) as Hci.
  pose proof (@committed_heap_item_obj_inv G D T0 hds Hci) as Hcdefs.
  pose proof (@committed_heap_defs_in D hds (heap_def_trm a (Some y)) Hcdefs Hin) as Hcd.
  pose proof (@committed_heap_def_trm_some_binds D a y Hcd) as Hycomm.
  exists (empty:ctx), D, (ℰ :: ℰs), (effs :: effss0).
  rewrite concat_empty_r.
  eapply (@ty_config_c G D Sigma ℰ ℰs Fs (trm_var (avar_f y)) Ts committed U nil effs effss0).
  - exact Hinert.
  - exact Hinits.
  - exact Hhc.
  - exact Hfs.
  - exact Hstack.
  - exact HyTs.
  - apply eff_ignore.
  - eapply init_var_binds. apply init_var_commit. exact Hycomm.
  - exact Hcorr.
Qed.

End Params.

  (effss:list effects) (Fs:stack) (Sigma:heap) (U:typ)
  (f z:var) (Tf:typ) (tf:trm),
  ty_config G D Es effss (trm_app (avar_f f) (avar_f z) ; Fs ; Sigma) U ->
  binds f (item_lit (lit_fun Tf tf)) Sigma ->

    ty_config (G & G') D' Es' effss' (open z tf ; Fs ; Sigma) U.
Proof.
  intros G D Es effss Fs Sigma U f z Tf tf Hcfg Hbitem.
  destruct (@ty_config_inv_s G D Es effss (trm_app (avar_f f) (avar_f z)) Fs Sigma U Hcfg) as
    (ℰ & ℰs & Ts & ii & effs & effs' & effss0 &
     HeqEs & HeqEffs & Hinert & Hinits & Hhc & Hfs & Hstack & Hty & Heff & Hinit & Hcorr).
  assert (Heffnil : effs' = nil) by (eapply eff_trm_app_nil; exact Heff).
  subst effs'. cbn in Hcorr. cbn in HeqEffs.
  destruct (@ty_app_inv G f z Ts Hty) as [S [Ut [Hfapp [HzS HopenSub]]]].
  destruct (@heap_correspond_lit G Sigma f (lit_fun Tf tf) Hhc Hbitem) as [T0 [HfG HlitTy]].
  assert (HinertT0 : inert_typ T0) by (eapply inert_binds_inert_typ; eassumption).
  destruct (@Hbind_all G f T0 S Ut Hinert HfG HinertT0 Hfapp)
    as [Sf [Uf [HeqT0 HsubAll]]].
  destruct (@ty_lit_fun_type_inv G Tf tf T0 HlitTy) as [Ubody HeqBody].
  assert (HeqAll : typ_all Tf Ubody = typ_all Sf Uf) by (rewrite <- HeqBody; exact HeqT0).
  injection HeqAll as HeqSf HeqUf. subst Sf Uf.
  assert (HbodyTy : exists L, forall x, x \notin L ->
            G & x ~ Tf ⊢ open x tf ∶ open x Ubody)
    by (eapply ty_lit_fun_body; exact HlitTy).
  destruct HbodyTy as [Lb HbodyTy].
  destruct (@Hall_inv G Tf Ubody S Ut Hinert HsubAll) as [La [HSsub HbodySub]].
  assert (HzTf : G ⊢ trm_var (avar_f z) ∶ Tf)
    by (eapply ty_sub; [exact HzS|exact HSsub]).
  assert (HopenTy : G ⊢ open z tf ∶ open z Ubody)
    by (eapply @ty_all_intro_open with (L:=Lb) (G:=G) (S:=Tf) (U:=Ubody) (t:=tf) (a:=z);
        [exact HbodyTy|exact HzTf]).
  assert (HopenSubU : G ⊢ open z Ubody <: open z Ut)
    by (eapply @subtyp_all_inst with (L:=La) (G:=G) (S2:=Tf) (U1:=Ubody) (U2:=Ut) (z:=z);
        [exact HbodySub|exact HzTf]).
  assert (HopenUt : G ⊢ open z Ubody <: open z Ut) by exact HopenSubU.
  assert (HyTs : G ⊢ open z tf ∶ Ts).
  { eapply ty_sub; [exact HopenTy|].
    eapply subtyp_trans; [exact HopenSubU|exact HopenSub]. }
  destruct (@init_app_commit G D (dom ℰ) f z ii Hinit) as [Hi Hcapp].
  subst ii.
  destruct (@commit_app_binds G D f z Hcapp) as [Hfcomm Hzcomm].
  pose proof (@free_sub_heaps_well_committed G D Sigma (ℰ :: ℰs) Hfs) as Hwc.
  pose proof (@well_committed_heap_item G D Sigma f (item_lit (lit_fun Tf tf)) Hwc Hfcomm Hbitem) as Hci.
  pose proof (@committed_heap_item_lit_inv G D (lit_fun Tf tf) Hci) as Hclit.
  destruct (@commit_lit_fun_body G D Tf tf Hclit) as [Lc HcommitBody].
  assert (HcommitOpen : G ⸴ D ⊢c open z tf)
    by (eapply @commit_all_intro_open with (L:=Lc) (G:=G) (D:=D) (S:=Tf) (t:=tf) (a:=z);
        [exact HcommitBody|exact HzTf|exact Hzcomm]).
  exists (empty:ctx), D, (ℰ :: ℰs), (effs :: effss0).
  rewrite concat_empty_r.
  eapply (@ty_config_c G D Sigma ℰ ℰs Fs (open z tf) Ts committed U nil effs effss0).
  - exact Hinert.
  - exact Hinits.
  - exact Hhc.
  - exact Hfs.
  - exact Hstack.
  - exact HyTs.
  - apply eff_ignore.
  - eapply init_commit. exact HcommitOpen.
  - exact Hcorr.
Qed.

End Params.

Unset Implicit Arguments.

Section Params.

(* Canonical shape of the binding of a variable typed at a universal type,
   in an inert context. *)
Hypothesis Hbind_all : forall (G:ctx) (f:var) (T0:typ) (S U:typ),
  inert G ->
  binds f T0 G ->
  inert_typ T0 ->
  G ⊢ trm_var (avar_f f) ∶ typ_all S U ->
  exists Sf Uf, T0 = typ_all Sf Uf /\
                G ⊢ typ_all Sf Uf <: typ_all S U.

(* Inversion of subtyping between universal types in an inert context. *)
Hypothesis Hall_inv : forall (G:ctx) (Sf Uf S U:typ),
  inert G ->
  G ⊢ typ_all Sf Uf <: typ_all S U ->
  exists L, G ⊢ S <: Sf /\
            (forall x, x \notin L -> G & x ~ Sf ⊢ open x Uf <: open x U).

Lemma ty_config_red_app : forall (G:ctx) (D:init_ctx) (Es:list eff_ctx)
  (effss:list effects) (Fs:stack) (Sigma:heap) (U:typ)
  (f z:var),
  ty_config G D Es effss (trm_app (avar_f f) (avar_f z) ; Fs ; Sigma) U ->
  exists G' D' Es' effss',
    ty_config (G & G') D' Es' effss'
      (open z (lit_body_of_app f)) Fs Sigma U.
Abort.

End Params.

Lemma open_rec_avar_b_eq : forall (n:nat) (x:var), open_rec n x (avar_b n) = avar_f x.
Proof. intros. unfold open_rec. cbn. rewrite If_l; auto. Qed.

Lemma open_rec_avar_b_neq : forall (n m:nat) (x:var), m <> n -> open_rec m x (avar_b n) = avar_b n.
Proof. intros. unfold open_rec. cbn. rewrite If_r; auto. Qed.

Lemma open_rec_avar_f : forall (n:nat) (x y:var), open_rec n x (avar_f y) = avar_f y.
Proof. intros. unfold open_rec. cbn. reflexivity. Qed.

Lemma subst_avar_b : forall (x y:var) (n:nat), subst_var x y (avar_b n) = avar_b n.
Proof. intros. unfold subst_var. cbn. reflexivity. Qed.

Lemma subst_avar_f : forall (x y z:var), subst_var x y (avar_f z) = avar_f (z \[x -> y]).
Proof. intros. unfold subst_var. cbn. reflexivity. Qed.

Lemma subst_avar_fresh : forall (x y:var) (a:avar), x \notin fv a -> subst_var x y a = a.
Proof.
  intros. destruct a as [n|z].
  - rewrite subst_avar_b. reflexivity.
  - rewrite subst_avar_f. f_equal. simpl in H.
    apply notin_singleton_r in H.
    rewrite If_r; auto.
Qed.

Lemma length_s_subst_typs : forall (x y:var) (Ts:typs), length_s (subst_var x y Ts) = length_s Ts.
Proof.
  intros x y Ts. induction Ts as [|T Ts IH]; simpl; auto.
Qed.

Require Import Base.
Require Import Case.
Require Import LibExtra.
Require Import Coq.Lists.List.
Require Import AbstractSyntax PreTyping Typing GeneralTyping RecordTypes InertTypes DefRecordInertTyping HeapCorrespondence OperationalSemantics Effects Initialization InitTyping InitLookup ConfigTyping.
Require Import CommittedSubHeap FreeSubHeapSingle FreeSubHeapStack StackTyping InertInitContexts InitWeakening EffectCorrespondence HeapEffects HeapDefsPointsTo WellPointed FreeItems PreciseTyping HeapUpdate.

Unset Implicit Arguments.

Lemma binds_split_fresh : forall (A:Type) (E:env A) (x:var) (v:A),
  binds x v E -> exists E1 E2, E = E1 & x ~ v & E2 /\ x # E2.
Proof.
  intros A E. induction E as [|[y w] E'].
  - intros x v Hb. inversion Hb.
  - intros x v Hb.
    change (binds x v (E' & y ~ w)) in Hb.
    destruct (LibEnv.binds_push_inv Hb) as [[E1 E2]|Hneq].
    + subst x v. exists E', empty. split.
      * rewrite concat_empty_r. reflexivity.
      * rewrite (@dom_empty A). apply notin_empty.
    + destruct Hneq as [Hne HbE'].
      destruct (IHE' x v HbE') as [E1 [E2 [Heq Hfresh]]].
      exists E1, (E2 & y ~ w). split.
      * rewrite Heq. rewrite <- concat_assoc. reflexivity.
      * intro Hz. rewrite dom_push in Hz. rewrite in_union in Hz.
        destruct Hz as [Hz|Hz].
        -- rewrite in_singleton in Hz. exact (Hne (eq_sym Hz)).
        -- exact (Hfresh Hz).
Qed.
