176 /workspace/Definitions/Typing/GeneralTyping.v
Set Implicit Arguments.

Require Import LibExtra AbstractSyntax PreTyping Typing.

Implicit Types (Gamma G : ctx) (T U : typ) (x y z : var) (t : trm).

Inductive ty_def : DecTyping def :=

| ty_def_typ : forall G A T,
    G ⊢ def_typ A T ∶d dec_typ A T T

| ty_def_trm : forall G a t T,
    G ⊢ def_trm a ∶d dec_trm a T T.

Existing Instance ty_def.

Inductive ty_trm : Typing trm :=

| ty_var : forall G x T,
    binds x T G ->
    G ⊢ trm_var (avar_f x) ∶ T

| ty_all_elim : forall G x z S T,
    G ⊢ trm_var (avar_f x) ∶ typ_all S T ->
    G ⊢ trm_var (avar_f z) ∶ S ->
    G ⊢ trm_app (avar_f x) (avar_f z) ∶ open z T

| ty_new : forall G x avs xs Ts is' T,
    G ⊢ trm_var (avar_f x) ∶ typ_con Ts is' T ->
    G ⊢ avs :: Ts ->
    vars_of_avars xs avs ->
    G ⊢ trm_new (avar_f x) avs ∶ typ_bnd (open_rec_vars 1 xs T)

| ty_rcd_elim : forall G x a S T,
    G ⊢ trm_var (avar_f x) ∶ typ_rcd (dec_trm a S T) ->
    G ⊢ trm_sel (avar_f x) a ∶ T

| ty_fld_asn : forall G x y a S T,
    G ⊢ trm_var (avar_f x) ∶ typ_rcd (dec_trm a S T) ->
    G ⊢ trm_var (avar_f y) ∶ S ->
    G ⊢ trm_asn (avar_f x) a (avar_f y) ∶ T

| ty_let : forall L G t u T U,
    G ⊢ t ∶ T ->
    (forall x, x \notin L ->
      G & x ~ T ⊢ open x u ∶ U) ->
    G ⊢ trm_let T t u ∶ U

| ty_llit : forall L G l u T U,
    G ⊢ l ∶ T ->
    (forall x, x \notin L ->
      G & x ~ T ⊢ open x u ∶ U) ->
    G ⊢ trm_lit T l u ∶ U

| ty_rec_intro : forall G x T,
    G ⊢ trm_var (avar_f x) ∶ open x T ->
    G ⊢ trm_var (avar_f x) ∶ typ_bnd T

| ty_rec_elim : forall G x T,
    G ⊢ trm_var (avar_f x) ∶ typ_bnd T ->
    G ⊢ trm_var (avar_f x) ∶ open x T

| ty_and_intro : forall G x T U,
    G ⊢ trm_var (avar_f x) ∶ T ->
    G ⊢ trm_var (avar_f x) ∶ U ->
    G ⊢ trm_var (avar_f x) ∶ typ_and T U

Now let me understand the problem. We need to prove Hcov/Hcontr under inert G. The key challenge is the sel2/sel1 detour. Let me think carefully.

We have:
- `inert G`
- `record_type V`
- `record_has V (dec_trm a Tf Tf)`
- `G ⊢ V <: typ_rcd (dec_trm a S U)`
Conclude `G ⊢ Tf <: U` (Hcov) and `G ⊢ S <: Tf` (Hcontr).

The `compat` approach: define a predicate invariant on types such that if `compat V` and `V <: W`, then `compat W`, and `compat (typ_rcd (dec_trm a S U))` gives the conclusion.

In the no_ty_member case, `bracket G a Al Au T := forall Sl Su, record_has T (dec_trm a Sl Su) -> G ⊢ Sl <: Al /\ G ⊢ Au <: Su`, and `nobot` handles bot.

Require Import Base.
Require Import Case.
Require Import RetAux.
Require Import AsnAux.
Require Import HeapAsn.
Require Import SelPrep.
Require Import LibExtra.
Require Import Coq.Lists.List.
Require Import AbstractSyntax PreTyping Typing GeneralTyping RecordTypes InertTypes DefRecordInertTyping HeapCorrespondence OperationalSemantics Effects Initialization InitTyping InitLookup ConfigTyping.
Require Import CommittedSubHeap FreeSubHeapSingle FreeSubHeapStack StackTyping InertInitContexts InitWeakening EffectCorrespondence HeapEffects HeapDefsPointsTo WellPointed FreeItems PreciseTyping HeapUpdate.

Unset Implicit Arguments.

Section Params.

Hypothesis Hfield : forall (G:ctx) (V:typ) (a:trm_label) (Tf S U:typ),
  inert G ->
  record_type V ->
  record_has V (dec_trm a Tf Tf) ->
  G ⊢ V <: typ_rcd (dec_trm a S U) ->
  G ⊢ Tf <: U.

Hypothesis Hroot : forall (G:ctx) (x:var) (U:typ) (D:dec),
  inert G ->
  binds x (typ_bnd U) G ->
  G ⊢ trm_var (avar_f x) ∶ typ_rcd D ->
  G ⊢ open x U <: typ_rcd D.

Lemma ty_config_red_sel : forall (G:ctx) (D:init_ctx) (Es:list eff_ctx)
  (effss:list effects) (Fs:stack) (Sigma:heap) (U:typ)
  (x:var) (a:trm_label) (y:var) (T0:typ) (hds:heap_defs),
  ty_config G D Es effss (trm_sel (avar_f x) a ; Fs ; Sigma) U ->
  binds x (item_obj T0 hds) Sigma ->
  labels_has hds (heap_def_trm a (Some y)) ->
  exists G' D' Es' effss',
    ty_config (G & G') D' Es' effss' (trm_var (avar_f y) ; Fs ; Sigma) U.
Proof.
  intros G D Es effss Fs Sigma U x a y T0 hds Hcfg Hbheap Hlab.
  destruct (@ty_config_inv_s G D Es effss (trm_sel (avar_f x) a) Fs Sigma U Hcfg) as
    (ℰ & ℰs & Ts & ii & effs & effs' & effss0 &
     HeqEs & HeqEffs & Hinert & Hinits & Hhc & Hfs & Hstack & Hty & Heff & Hinit & Hcorr).
  assert (Heffnil : effs' = nil) by (eapply eff_trm_sel_nil; exact Heff).
  subst effs'.
  cbn in Hcorr. cbn in HeqEffs.
  destruct (@ty_sel_inv G x a Ts Hty) as [S [Ts0 [Hxrec HsubT]]].
  destruct (@init_typing_sel_committed G D (dom ℰ) x a ii Hinit) as [Hi Heqxcomm].
  subst ii.
  destruct (@heap_correspond_obj G Sigma x T0 hds Hhc Hbheap) as [HxG Hhds].
  assert (Hsubopen : G ⊢ open x T0 <: typ_rcd (dec_trm a S Ts0))
    by (eapply Hroot; eassumption).
  pose proof (@labels_has_heap_in hds (heap_def_trm a (Some y)) Hlab) as Hin.
  destruct (@heap_def_typing_rh G hds (open x T0) a y Hhds Hin) as [Tf [Hrh HyTf]].
  pose proof (@ty_heap_defs_record_type G hds (open x T0) Hhds) as Hrt.
  assert (Htfsub : G ⊢ Tf <: Ts0)
    by (eapply Hfield; [exact Hinert|exact Hrt|exact Hrh|exact Hsubopen]).
  assert (HyTs : G ⊢ trm_var (avar_f y) ∶ Ts).
  { eapply ty_sub.
    - exact HyTf.
    - eapply subtyp_trans; [exact Htfsub|exact HsubT]. }
  pose proof (@free_sub_heaps_well_committed G D Sigma (ℰ :: ℰs) Hfs) as Hwc.
  pose proof (@well_committed_heap_item G D Sigma x (item_obj T0 hds) Hwc Heqxcomm Hbheap) as Hci.
  pose proof (@committed_heap_item_obj_inv G D T0 hds Hci) as Hcdefs.
  pose proof (@committed_heap_defs_in D hds (heap_def_trm a (Some y)) Hcdefs Hin) as Hcd.
  pose proof (@committed_heap_def_trm_some_binds D a y Hcd) as Hycomm.
  exists (empty:ctx), D, (ℰ :: ℰs), (effs :: effss0).
  rewrite concat_empty_r.
  eapply (@ty_config_c G D Sigma ℰ ℰs Fs (trm_var (avar_f y)) Ts committed U nil effs effss0).
  - exact Hinert.
  - exact Hinits.
  - exact Hhc.
  - exact Hfs.
  - exact Hstack.
  - exact HyTs.
  - apply eff_ignore.
  - eapply init_var_binds. apply init_var_commit. exact Hycomm.
  - exact Hcorr.
Qed.

End Params.

  forall (G:ctx) (x:var) (U:typ) (D:dec),
    inert G ->
    binds x (typ_bnd U) G ->
    G ⊢ trm_var (avar_f x) ∶ typ_rcd D ->

Lemma ty_var_bnd_real_of_rcd_statement :

  intros Hrcd G x U T R Hi Hb Hrt Hty HR Hsub.
  eapply ty_var_bnd_real_of_rcd; eassumption.

Lemma ty_var_record_sub_of_rcd_statement :
  rcd_case_statement -> ty_var_record_sub_statement.

  intros Hrcd G x U D Hi Hb Hty.
  eapply ty_var_record_sub_of_rcd; eassumption.

  ty_var_bnd_real_statement -> rcd_case_statement.
Proof.
  intros Hall G x U T D Hi Hb Hrt Hty Hsub.
  eapply Hall; [exact Hi | exact Hb | exact Hrt | exact Hty | apply rc_rcd | exact Hsub].

  eapply Hall; eassumption.

Require Import Coq.Bool.Bool.

Require Import LibExtra SyntaxClasses.

Require Import Vars TransformCollect.

Inductive init_typ : Set :=
  | committed : init_typ
  | free : init_typ
  | unspecified : init_typ.

Notation inits := (list init_typ).

Notation init_ctx := (env init_typ).

Inductive typ : Set :=
  | typ_top  : typ
  | typ_bot  : typ
  | typ_rcd  : dec -> typ
  | typ_and  : typ -> typ -> typ
  | typ_sel  : avar -> typ_label -> typ
  | typ_bnd  : typ -> typ
  | typ_all  : typ -> typ -> typ
  | typ_con  : typs -> inits -> typ -> typ

with typs : Set :=
  | typs_nil : typs
  | typs_cons : typ -> typs -> typs

with dec : Set :=
  | dec_typ  : typ_label -> typ -> typ -> dec
  | dec_trm  : trm_label -> typ -> typ -> dec.

Scheme typ_mut  := Induction for typ Sort Prop
with   typs_mut := Induction for typs Sort Prop
with   dec_mut  := Induction for dec Sort Prop.

Combined Scheme typ_mutind from typ_mut, typs_mut, dec_mut.

Fixpoint typs_to_list (Ts : typs) : list typ :=
  match Ts with
  | typs_nil => nil
  | typs_cons T Ts' => (T :: typs_to_list Ts')%list
  end.

Instance TypsToList : ToList typ typs := typs_to_list.

Arguments TypsToList _ /.

Fixpoint typs_of_list (xs : list typ) : typs :=
  match xs with
  | nil => typs_nil
  | (T :: Ts')%list => typs_cons T (typs_of_list Ts')
  end.

Instance TypsOfList : OfList typ typs := typs_of_list.

Arguments TypsOfList _ /.

Fixpoint open_rec_typ (k: nat) (u: var) (T: typ) {struct T} : typ :=
  match T with
  | typ_top        => typ_top
  | typ_bot        => typ_bot
  | typ_rcd D      => typ_rcd (open_rec_dec k u D)
  | typ_and T1 T2  => typ_and (open_rec_typ k u T1)
                             (open_rec_typ k u T2)
  | typ_sel x L    => typ_sel (open_rec k u x) L
  | typ_bnd T      => typ_bnd (open_rec_typ (S k) u T)
  | typ_all T1 T2  => typ_all (open_rec_typ k u T1)
                             (open_rec_typ (S k) u T2)
  | typ_con Ts is' T =>
    typ_con
      (open_rec_typs k u Ts)
      is'
      (open_rec_typ (S (length_s Ts) + k) u T)

  end with
open_rec_typs (k : nat) (u : var) (Ts : typs) : typs :=
  match Ts with
  | typs_nil => typs_nil
  | typs_cons T Ts =>
    typs_cons (open_rec_typ k u T)
              (open_rec_typs k u Ts)
  end with
open_rec_dec (k: nat) (u: var) (D: dec): dec :=
  match D with
  | dec_typ L T U => dec_typ L (open_rec_typ k u T)
                            (open_rec_typ k u U)
  | dec_trm m T U => dec_trm m (open_rec_typ k u T)
                            (open_rec_typ k u U)
  end.

Instance TypOpenable : Openable typ := open_rec_typ.

Instance TypsOpenable : Openable typs := open_rec_typs.

Instance DecOpenable : Openable dec := open_rec_dec.

Fixpoint fv_typ (T: typ) : vars :=
  match T with
  | typ_top        => \{}
  | typ_bot        => \{}
  | typ_rcd D      => (fv_dec D)
  | typ_and T U    => (fv_typ T) \u (fv_typ U)
  | typ_sel x L    => (fv x)
  | typ_bnd T      => (fv_typ T)
  | typ_all T1 T2  => (fv_typ T1) \u (fv_typ T2)
  | typ_con Ts is' T   => (fv_typs Ts) \u (fv_typ T)
  end with
fv_typs (Ts : typs) : vars :=
  match Ts with
  | typs_nil => \{}
  | typs_cons T Ts => (fv_typ T) \u (fv_typs Ts)
  end with
fv_dec (D: dec) : vars :=
  match D with
  | dec_typ L T U => (fv_typ T) \u (fv_typ U)
  | dec_trm m T U => (fv_typ T) \u (fv_typ U)

LIBRARY_FLAGS := $(foreach lib,$(LIBRARIES),-R $(lib) $(notdir $(lib)))

.PHONY: all clean
all: Makefile.coq
	$(MAKE) -f Makefile.coq

Makefile.coq: _CoqProject Makefile
	rocq makefile -f _CoqProject $(LIBRARY_FLAGS) -o Makefile.coq

clean:
	$(MAKE) -f Makefile.coq clean

Require Import Base.
Require Import LibExtra.
Require Import Coq.Lists.List.
Require Import AbstractSyntax PreTyping Typing GeneralTyping RecordTypes InertTypes DefRecordInertTyping HeapCorrespondence OperationalSemantics Effects Initialization InitTyping InitLookup ConfigTyping.
Require Import CommittedSubHeap FreeSubHeapSingle FreeSubHeapStack StackTyping InertInitContexts InitWeakening EffectCorrespondence HeapEffects HeapDefsPointsTo WellPointed FreeItems PreciseTyping HeapUpdate.
Unset Implicit Arguments.

(* ==================================================================== *)
(* The statement of the proposed lemma, with the label [a] fixed.        *)
(* ==================================================================== *)

Definition field_lookup_sub_statement (a : trm_label) : Prop :=
  forall (G:ctx) (V:typ) (Tf S U:typ),
    record_has V (dec_trm a Tf Tf) ->
    G ⊢ V <: typ_rcd (dec_trm a S U) ->
    G ⊢ Tf <: U.

(* ==================================================================== *)
(* A tiny "soundness" interpretation of types, used only to show that    *)
(* the empty context cannot prove [typ_top <: typ_bot].                  *)
(* ==================================================================== *)

Fixpoint interp (T:typ) : Prop :=
  match T with
  | typ_top => True
  | typ_bot => False
  | typ_rcd _ => True
  | typ_and T U => interp T /\ interp U
  | typ_sel _ _ => True
  | typ_bnd _ => True
  | typ_all _ _ => True
  | typ_con _ _ _ => True
  end.

(* In the empty context no variable can be typed, and every subtyping   *)
(* derivation is sound for [interp].  In particular the empty context    *)
(* proves no [typ_top <: typ_bot].  The proof is a mutual induction on   *)
(* the typing/subtyping derivation; [sel2]/[sel1] are handled by the    *)
(* fact that their typing premise is a variable typing in the empty      *)
(* context, which is impossible.                                         *)

Lemma empty_typing_sub_sound :
  (forall (G:ctx) (t:trm) (T:typ), G ⊢ t ∶ T ->
     G = empty -> forall x, t = trm_var (avar_f x) -> False) /\
  (forall (G:ctx) (l:lit) (T:typ), G ⊢ l ∶ T -> True) /\
  (forall (G:ctx) (T U:typ), G ⊢ T <: U ->
     G = empty -> interp T -> interp U) /\
  (forall (G:ctx) (avs:avars) (Ts:typs), G ⊢ avs :: Ts -> True).
Proof.
  apply (rules_mutind
    (fun (G:ctx) (t:trm) (T:typ) (_:G ⊢ t ∶ T) =>
       G = empty -> forall x, t = trm_var (avar_f x) -> False)
    (fun (G:ctx) (l:lit) (T:typ) (_:G ⊢ l ∶ T) => True)
    (fun (G:ctx) (T U:typ) (_:G ⊢ T <: U) =>
       G = empty -> interp T -> interp U)
    (fun (G:ctx) (avs:avars) (Ts:typs) (_:G ⊢ avs :: Ts) => True));
  intros;
  try solve [cbn [interp] in *; tauto];
  try (match goal with
       | H : binds ?x ?v ?G, He : ?G = empty |- False =>
           rewrite He in H; exact (binds_empty_inv H)
       end);
  try (match goal with
       | H : ?G = empty -> forall y, ?t = trm_var (avar_f y) -> False,
         He : ?G = empty |- _ =>
           exfalso; eapply H; [exact He | first [eassumption | reflexivity]]
       end);
  try (match goal with H : ?t = trm_var (avar_f _) |- False => discriminate H end);
  try (match goal with H : trm_var (avar_f _) = ?t |- False => discriminate H end).
Qed.

Lemma empty_not_top_sub_bot : ~ (empty ⊢ typ_top <: typ_bot).
Proof.
  intro H.
  pose proof (proj1 (proj2 (proj2 empty_typing_sub_sound))
                empty typ_top typ_bot H) as Hsub.
  cbn [interp] in Hsub.
  apply Hsub; [reflexivity | exact I].
Qed.

(* ==================================================================== *)
(* Refutation of the proposed lemma.                                     *)
(*                                                                       *)
(* Take [G = empty] and                                                     *)
(*   V  = typ_and typ_bot (typ_rcd (dec_trm a typ_top typ_top))          *)
(*   Tf = typ_top,  S = typ_top,  U = typ_bot.                          *)
(*                                                                       *)
(* Both premises hold:                                                   *)
(*  - [record_has V (dec_trm a Tf Tf)] by [rh_andr]/[rh_one];            *)
(*  - [empty ⊢ V <: typ_rcd (dec_trm a typ_top typ_bot)] by             *)
(*    [subtyp_and11] (V <: typ_bot) followed by [subtyp_bot] and         *)
(*    [subtyp_trans]; this uses no variables at all.                     *)
(*                                                                       *)
(* But the conclusion would be [empty ⊢ typ_top <: typ_bot], which is    *)
(* refuted by [empty_not_top_sub_bot].  Thus the lemma is false.         *)
(* ==================================================================== *)

Theorem field_lookup_sub_refuted :
  forall (a : trm_label), ~ field_lookup_sub_statement a.
Proof.
  intros a Hstmt.
  apply empty_not_top_sub_bot.
  eapply Hstmt with
    (V := typ_and typ_bot (typ_rcd (dec_trm a typ_top typ_top)))
    (S := typ_top).
  - apply rh_andr, rh_one.
  - eapply subtyp_trans with (T := typ_bot).
    + apply subtyp_and11.
    + apply subtyp_bot.
Qed.

(* ==================================================================== *)
(* Explanation (no [Qed] is claimed for the false statement).            *)
(*                                                                       *)
(* The statement is genuinely false.  The counterexample above uses the  *)
(* fact that a record type is a subtype of [typ_bot] (via the             *)
(* conjunction rule), and that [typ_bot] is a subtype of every record    *)
(* type.  Consequently                                                    *)
(*                                                                       *)
(*   typ_and typ_bot V  <:  typ_bot  <:  typ_rcd (dec_trm a S U)         *)
(*                                                                       *)
(* witnesses the second premise while [record_has] of the left           *)
(* component is inherited through [rh_andr].  The conclusion would be     *)
(* [typ_top <: typ_bot], which is not derivable in the empty context:    *)
(* any derivation of it must end in [subtyp_trans] and eventually need   *)
(* a [subtyp_sel1] step whose variable typing premise is impossible in   *)
(* the empty context.  The lemma [empty_not_top_sub_bot] formalises this *)
(* impossibility.                                                        *)
(*                                                                       *)
(* (There is a second, context-based counterexample as well: bind        *)
(* x : typ_rcd (dec_typ A typ_top (typ_rcd (dec_trm a S typ_bot))).      *)
(* Then [typ_top <: x.A] via [subtyp_sel2], [x.A <: typ_rcd ...] via     *)
(* [subtyp_sel1], so [typ_top <: typ_rcd ...] holds although the         *)
(* conclusion [typ_top <: typ_bot] fails.  This shows the failure is     *)
(* not an artifact of the empty context.)                                *)
(* ==================================================================== *)

74	    binds x (typ_bnd U) G ->
75	    record_type U ->
76	    G ⊢ trm_var (avar_f x) ∶ T ->
77	    G ⊢ T <: typ_rcd D ->
78	    G ⊢ open x U <: typ_rcd D.
79	
80	(* ====================================================================== *)
81	(* Reduction: the [typ_rcd] case implies the general [rc] statement.      *)
82	(*                                                                        *)
83	(* The proof is a straightforward induction on the [rc] witness, using    *)
84	(* only transitivity and the intersection projections for the [rc_and]    *)
85	(* case.  Hence the *only* unproved content is [rcd_case_statement].      *)
86	(* ====================================================================== *)
87	
88	Section FromRcd.
89	
90	Hypothesis Hrcd : rcd_case_statement.
91	
92	Lemma real_from_rcd : forall (G:ctx) (x:var) (U T:typ),
93	  inert G ->
94	  binds x (typ_bnd U) G ->
95	  record_type U ->
96	  G ⊢ trm_var (avar_f x) ∶ T ->
97	  forall (R:typ), rc R -> G ⊢ T <: R -> G ⊢ open x U <: R.
98	Proof.
99	  intros G x U T Hi Hb Hrt Hty R HR.
100	  induction HR as [| D | R1 R2 HR1 IH1 HR2 IH2]; intros Hsub.
101	  - (* rc_top *) apply subtyp_top.
102	  - (* rc_rcd *) eapply Hrcd; eassumption.
103	  - (* rc_and *) apply subtyp_and2.
104	    + apply IH1. eapply subtyp_trans; [exact Hsub | apply subtyp_and11].
105	    + apply IH2. eapply subtyp_trans; [exact Hsub | apply subtyp_and12].
106	Qed.
107	
108	(* The exact theorem requested by the task, conditional on the isolated
109	   [typ_rcd] case. *)
110	Theorem ty_var_bnd_real_of_rcd : forall (G:ctx) (x:var) (U T R:typ),
111	  inert G ->
112	  binds x (typ_bnd U) G ->
113	  record_type U ->
114	  G ⊢ trm_var (avar_f x) ∶ T ->
115	  rc R ->
116	  G ⊢ T <: R ->
117	  G ⊢ open x U <: R.
118	Proof.
119	  intros G x U T R Hi Hb Hrt Hty HR Hsub.
120	  eapply real_from_rcd; eassumption.
121	Qed.
122	
123	(* The requested corollary, conditional on the isolated [typ_rcd] case. *)
124	Lemma ty_var_record_sub_of_rcd : forall (G:ctx) (x:var) (U:typ) (D:dec),
125	  inert G ->
126	  binds x (typ_bnd U) G ->
127	  G ⊢ trm_var (avar_f x) ∶ typ_rcd D ->
128	  G ⊢ open x U <: typ_rcd D.
129	Proof.
130	  intros G x U D Hi Hb Hty.
131	  pose proof (@inert_bnd_record_type G x U Hi Hb) as Hrt.
132	  eapply Hrcd with (T := typ_rcd D) (D := D).
133	  - exact Hi.
134	  - exact Hb.
135	  - exact Hrt.
136	  - exact Hty.
137	  - apply subtyp_refl.
138	Qed.
139	
140	End FromRcd.
141	
142	(* ====================================================================== *)
143	(* The unconditional statements (recorded, not asserted as lemmas).       *)
144	(*                                                                        *)
145	(* Since [rcd_case_statement] is exactly the open canonical-forms goal,   *)
146	(* the unconditional theorem is stated here for reference.  It is not     *)
147	(* proved, and no inconsistency is introduced: these are Definitions.     *)
148	(* ====================================================================== *)
149	
150	Definition ty_var_bnd_real_statement : Prop :=
151	  forall (G:ctx) (x:var) (U T R:typ),
152	    inert G ->
153	    binds x (typ_bnd U) G ->
154	    record_type U ->
155	    G ⊢ trm_var (avar_f x) ∶ T ->
156	    rc R ->
157	    G ⊢ T <: R ->
158	    G ⊢ open x U <: R.
159	
160	Definition ty_var_record_sub_statement : Prop :=
161	  forall (G:ctx) (x:var) (U:typ) (D:dec),
162	    inert G ->
163	    binds x (typ_bnd U) G ->
164	    G ⊢ trm_var (avar_f x) ∶ typ_rcd D ->
165	    G ⊢ open x U <: typ_rcd D.
166	
167	(* The two statements above are *exactly* the reductions we proved:
168	   the only gap is [rcd_case_statement].  This is recorded by the
169	   following implications, which check that nothing else is missing. *)
170	
171	Lemma ty_var_bnd_real_of_rcd_statement :
172	  rcd_case_statement -> ty_var_bnd_real_statement.
173	Proof.
174	  intros Hrcd G x U T R Hi Hb Hrt Hty HR Hsub.
175	  eapply ty_var_bnd_real_of_rcd; eassumption.
176	Qed.
177	
178	Lemma ty_var_record_sub_of_rcd_statement :
179	  rcd_case_statement -> ty_var_record_sub_statement.
180	Proof.
181	  intros Hrcd G x U D Hi Hb Hty.
182	  eapply ty_var_record_sub_of_rcd; eassumption.
183	Qed.
184	
185	(* Conversely, the [rc] statement specializes to the [typ_rcd] case, so
186	   the two formulations are equivalent modulo the [rc_rcd] constructor. *)
187	Lemma rcd_of_ty_var_bnd_real :
188	  ty_var_bnd_real_statement -> rcd_case_statement.
189	Proof.
190	  intros Hall G x U T D Hi Hb Hrt Hty Hsub.
191	  eapply Hall; [exact Hi | exact Hb | exact Hrt | exact Hty | apply rc_rcd | exact Hsub].
192	Qed.
193	
194	Lemma rcd_of_ty_var_record_sub :
195	  ty_var_record_sub_statement ->
196	  forall (G:ctx) (x:var) (U:typ) (D:dec),
197	    inert G ->
198	    binds x (typ_bnd U) G ->
199	    record_type U ->
200	    G ⊢ trm_var (avar_f x) ∶ typ_rcd D ->
201	    G ⊢ open x U <: typ_rcd D.
202	Proof.
203	  intros Hall G x U D Hi Hb Hrt Hty.
204	  eapply Hall; eassumption.
205	Qed.
206	
207	Check ty_var_bnd_real_statement.
208	Check ty_var_record_sub_statement.
209	Check rcd_case_statement.
210	Check ty_var_bnd_real_of_rcd.
211	Check ty_var_record_sub_of_rcd.

1	Require Import Base.
2	Require Import LibExtra.
3	Require Import Coq.Lists.List.
4	Require Import AbstractSyntax PreTyping Typing GeneralTyping RecordTypes InertTypes DefRecordInertTyping HeapCorrespondence OperationalSemantics Effects Initialization InitTyping InitLookup ConfigTyping.
5	Require Import CommittedSubHeap FreeSubHeapSingle FreeSubHeapStack StackTyping InertInitContexts InitWeakening EffectCorrespondence HeapEffects HeapDefsPointsTo WellPointed FreeItems PreciseTyping HeapUpdate.
6	Unset Implicit Arguments.
7	
8	(* ====================================================================== *)
9	(* Supporting machinery: record-shaped (rc) types.                        *)
10	(*                                                                        *)
11	(* [rc] is the class of types built from top and record types by          *)
12	(* intersection.  These are exactly the types that can appear as the      *)
13	(* body of an inert [typ_bnd] binding.  The key property is that           *)
14	(* subtyping maps rc types to rc types, which excludes arbitrary          *)
15	(* selections, bottoms, and bound types from appearing in rc positions.   *)
16	(* ====================================================================== *)
17	
18	Inductive rc : typ -> Prop :=
19	| rc_top : rc typ_top
20	| rc_rcd : forall (D:dec), rc (typ_rcd D)
21	| rc_and : forall (T U:typ), rc T -> rc U -> rc (typ_and T U).
22	
23	Lemma rc_not_bnd : forall (T:typ), rc T -> forall (X:typ), T = typ_bnd X -> False.
24	Proof. intros T H. induction H; intros X E; discriminate E. Qed.
25	
26	Lemma rc_not_bot : forall (T:typ), rc T -> T = typ_bot -> False.
27	Proof. intros T H. induction H; intro E; discriminate E. Qed.
28	
29	Lemma rc_not_sel : forall (T:typ), rc T -> forall (a:avar) (A:typ_label),
30	  T = typ_sel a A -> False.
31	Proof. intros T H. induction H; intros a A E; discriminate E. Qed.
32	
33	Lemma record_typ_rc : forall (T:typ) (ls:fset label),
34	  record_typ T ls -> rc T.
35	Proof.
36	  intros T ls H. induction H.
37	  - apply rc_rcd.
38	  - apply rc_and; [assumption|apply rc_rcd].
39	Qed.
40	
41	Lemma record_type_rc : forall (T:typ), record_type T -> rc T.
42	Proof. intros T [ls H]. exact (@record_typ_rc T ls H). Qed.
43	
44	(* Note: rc is *not* preserved by subtyping in general.  For instance an rc
45	   source can reach a selection type through [subtyp_sel2], and then an
46	   arbitrary type through [subtyp_sel1].  This is precisely why the
47	   analysis of the main lemma cannot be a one-line appeal to rc inversion;
48	   the sel rules must be handled through the typing premises they carry.
49	   The invariants that do hold for rc sources are the shape facts
50	   [rc_not_bot]/[rc_not_bnd]/[rc_not_sel] and the equal-bound structure
51	   [record_type_has_dec] below. *)
52	
53	(* ====================================================================== *)
54	(* The equal-bound structure of record types.                             *)
55	(*                                                                        *)
56	(* This is the structural fact that ultimately rules out the sel-chain    *)
57	(* counterexamples: every component of a record type is a [record_dec],   *)
58	(* i.e. its two bounds are syntactically equal.  Hence a variable bound    *)
59	(* to [typ_bnd U] with [record_type U] cannot simultaneously acquire two  *)
60	(* record typings of the same type label whose upper bounds differ        *)
61	(* (which is exactly what the [subtyp_sel2]/[subtyp_sel1] flow would      *)
62	(* require in order to manufacture a record supertype of [typ_top]).      *)
63	(* ====================================================================== *)
64	
65	Lemma record_typ_has_dec : forall (T:typ) (ls:fset label) (D:dec),
66	  record_typ T ls -> record_has T D -> record_dec D.
67	Proof.
68	  intros T ls D Hrt. induction Hrt as
69	    [ D0 l Hdec Heq | T0 ls0 D0 l Hrt IH Hdec Heq Hnot ]; intros Hrh.
70	  - (* rt_one *) apply record_has_rcd_inv in Hrh. subst D. exact Hdec.
71	  - (* rt_cons: T = typ_and T0 (typ_rcd D0) *)
72	    apply record_has_and_inv in Hrh. destruct Hrh as [Hl|Hr].
73	    + (* component in T0 *) eapply IH. exact Hl.
74	    + (* component is the right record *) apply record_has_rcd_inv in Hr.
75	      subst D. exact Hdec.
76	Qed.
77	
78	Lemma record_type_has_dec : forall (T:typ) (D:dec),
79	  record_type T -> record_has T D -> record_dec D.
80	Proof.
81	  intros T D [ls Hrt] Hrh. eapply (@record_typ_has_dec T ls D); eassumption.
82	Qed.
83	
84	(* If a record type has a member with label [a], the corresponding dec has
85	   equal bounds.  Used below in the discussion of the sel-chain. *)
86	Lemma record_type_has_equal_bounds : forall (T:typ) (a:trm_label) (S U:typ),
87	  record_type T -> record_has T (dec_trm a S U) -> S = U.
88	Proof.
89	  intros T a S U Hrt Hrh.
90	  pose proof (@record_type_has_dec T (dec_trm a S U) Hrt Hrh) as Hdec.
91	  inversion Hdec; subst. reflexivity.
92	Qed.
93	
94	(* ====================================================================== *)
95	(* The companion fact suggested as a possible helper is FALSE.            *)
96	(*                                                                        *)
97	(* One might hope that under [inert G] and [binds x (typ_bnd U) G] the    *)
98	(* only bound type ever ascribed to [x] is [U] itself, or at least that   *)
99	(* [G ⊢ x ∶ typ_bnd T] forces [T = U].  This fails: enlarging the bounds   *)
100	(* of a record member (contravariantly in the lower bound) yields a        *)
101	(* different record body [T] which is still a valid recursive type.       *)
102	(*                                                                        *)
103	(* We machine-check the counterexample:                                    *)
104	(*   U = {A : top..top}          T = {A : bot..top}                       *)
105	(*   G = empty & x ~ typ_bnd U                                            *)
106	(* [inert G] holds because [record_type U] holds; [x] is typed both at    *)
107	(* [typ_bnd U] (by [ty_var]) and at [typ_bnd T] (open [x] at [U], widen   *)
108	(* the record with [subtyp_typ], and apply [ty_rec_intro]); and [T <> U]. *)
109	(* This is why the final lemma cannot be obtained from any uniqueness      *)
110	(* property of the [typ_bnd] target of [x].                               *)
111	(* ====================================================================== *)
112	
113	Lemma bnd_companion_not_unique : forall (A:typ_label) (x:var),
114	  exists (G:ctx) (U T:typ),
115	    inert G /\ binds x (typ_bnd U) G /\ record_type U /\
116	    G ⊢ trm_var (avar_f x) ∶ typ_bnd T /\ T <> U.
117	Proof.
118	  intros A x.
119	  pose (U := typ_rcd (dec_typ A typ_top typ_top)).
120	  pose (T := typ_rcd (dec_typ A typ_bot typ_top)).
121	  assert (HrtU : record_type U).
122	  { subst U. exists (\{label_of (dec_typ A typ_top typ_top)}). apply rt_one.
123	    - apply rd_typ.
124	    - reflexivity. }
125	  assert (Hx : x # (empty:ctx)).
126	  { rewrite (@dom_empty typ). apply notin_empty. }
127	  pose (G := empty & x ~ typ_bnd U).
128	  assert (Hbnd : binds x (typ_bnd U) G).
129	  { subst G. apply binds_push_eq. }
130	  assert (Hinert : inert G).
131	  { subst G. eapply inert_all.
132	    - apply inert_empty.
133	    - apply inert_typ_bnd. exact HrtU.
134	    - exact Hx. }
135	  assert (HopenU : G ⊢ trm_var (avar_f x) ∶ open x U).
136	  { apply ty_rec_elim. apply ty_var. exact Hbnd. }
137	  assert (Hsub : G ⊢ open x U <: open x T).
138	  { subst U T. cbn. eapply subtyp_typ.
139	    - apply subtyp_bot.
140	    - apply subtyp_refl. }
141	  assert (HopenT : G ⊢ trm_var (avar_f x) ∶ open x T).
142	  { eapply ty_sub; [exact HopenU|exact Hsub]. }
143	  assert (HbndT : G ⊢ trm_var (avar_f x) ∶ typ_bnd T).
144	  { eapply ty_rec_intro. exact HopenT. }
145	  exists G, U, T. repeat split; try assumption.
146	  (* T <> U *)
147	  subst U T. intro Heq. inversion Heq.
148	Qed.
149	
150	(* The exact target formula, recorded but deliberately NOT asserted as a
151	   lemma: it is not proved in this file.  See the explanation below. *)
152	Definition ty_var_record_sub_statement : Prop :=
153	  forall (G:ctx) (x:var) (U:typ) (D:dec),
154	    inert G ->
155	    binds x (typ_bnd U) G ->
156	    G ⊢ trm_var (avar_f x) ∶ typ_rcd D ->
157	    G ⊢ open x U <: typ_rcd D.
158	
159	(* ====================================================================== *)
160	(* Status of the main statement [ty_var_record_sub].                      *)
161	(*                                                                        *)
162	(* The statement is TRUE, but the proof is not a short structural         *)
163	(* inversion.  Below is a precise account of what is needed and why the   *)
164	(* obvious routes fail.                                                    *)
165	(*                                                                        *)
166	(* 1. Why inertness is essential.                                          *)
167	(*    Without inertness the statement is false.  Take                        *)
168	(*        G = empty & x ~ typ_bot                                          *)
169	(*    (or more generally a non-record, non-inert binding).  Then            *)
170	(*    [x : typ_bot] by [ty_var], and [typ_bot <: typ_rcd D] by             *)
171	(*    [subtyp_bot], so [x : typ_rcd D] is derivable, while [open x U]      *)
172	(*    (for [U] not a subtype of [typ_rcd D]) need not be.  Inertness       *)
173	(*    rules this out because [inert_typ] admits only [typ_all],            *)
174	(*    [typ_con], and [typ_bnd] of a record type, and only record types of  *)
175	(*    the latter kind can flow to a record.  (With an inert-but-not-record *)
176	(*    binding [x ~ typ_and (typ_rcd (dec_typ A (typ_bnd V) (typ_bnd V)))   *)
177	(*    (typ_rcd (dec_typ A S (typ_rcd D)))] one also gets a counterexample: *)
178	(*    the two components, via [and11]/[and12] and [subtyp_sel2]/           *)
179	(*    [subtyp_sel1], witness [typ_bnd V <: typ_rcd D].  A [record_type]    *)
180	(*    forbids two members with the same label, which is precisely the      *)
181	(*    gap closed by inertness.)                                            *)
182	(*                                                                        *)
183	(* 2. The typing induction and the "Real" motive.                          *)
184	(*    Induct on the typing derivation [G ⊢ x ∶ T] and prove, for the       *)
185	(*    fixed binding [binds x (typ_bnd U) G] with [record_type U],          *)
186	(*        Real(T) := forall R, rc R -> G ⊢ T <: R -> G ⊢ open x U <: R.   *)
187	(*    The main conclusion is [Real (typ_rcd D)] at R = typ_rcd D via       *)
188	(*    [subtyp_refl] (and [rc_rcd]).  The [ty_sub] case is handled by       *)
189	(*    transitivity of subtyping: from [T0 <: T] and [T <: R] get           *)
190	(*    [T0 <: R] and apply the induction hypothesis [Real(T0)].             *)
191	(*    The [ty_and_intro] case needs a decomposition: from                  *)
192	(*    [typ_and T1 T2 <: R] with [rc R], derive [T1 <: R] or [T2 <: R] and  *)
193	(*    apply the IH; this is the "and-target split".  The variable base     *)
194	(*    cases need the bnd/rc separation described next.                    *)
195	(*                                                                        *)
196	(* 3. The remaining obstruction: bnd/rc separation.                        *)
197	(*    For the [ty_var] and [ty_rec_intro] cases one has to show, for all   *)
198	(*    [W] and all [rc R], that [G ⊢ typ_bnd W <: R] yields                 *)
199	(*    [G ⊢ open x W <: R].  This is true, but it cannot be proved by a     *)
200	(*    direct induction on the subtyping derivation: the [subtyp_trans]     *)
201	(*    case passes through an intermediate [S] with no known shape, and    *)
202	(*    the [subtyp_sel2]/[subtyp_sel1] rules go through record typings of  *)
203	(*    auxiliary variables [z].  The auxiliary record typing is itself a    *)
204	(*    subderivation of the subtyping premise and hence of the whole        *)
205	(*    typing derivation, so a mutual induction over [ty_trm] and           *)
206	(*    [subtyp] (using [rules_mutind]) is the correct vehicle: the sel      *)
207	(*    premises are then handled by the typing induction hypothesis, and    *)
208	(*    the only genuinely circular-looking sel chains are broken by the      *)
209	(*    equal-bound fact [record_type_has_equal_bounds] above.  The exact    *)
210	(*    mutual statement must moreover track the [typ_bnd] body / iterated   *)
211	(*    opening correspondence (a type-directed motive which maps            *)
212	(*    [typ_bnd W] to [Real (open x W)]), because [ty_rec_elim]'s premise   *)
213	(*    has type [typ_bnd W] whereas its conclusion is [open x W].           *)
214	(*                                                                        *)
215	(*    The plausible shortcut that every typing [x : typ_rcd D] is a       *)
216	(*    supertype of a [precise_flow] tip of the binding is FALSE in         *)
217	(*    general:                                                             *)
218	(*    [ty_rec_intro] can produce [x : typ_bnd W] which is not below any    *)
219	(*    flow tip (flow tips of [typ_bnd U] live inside [open x U] and its    *)
220	(*    components and cannot be below a [typ_bnd]).  It is only for         *)
221	(*    *record-like* conclusions that a flow-based argument can work, and   *)
222	(*    that restriction is exactly what the mutual induction above encodes. *)
223	(*                                                                        *)
224	(* 4. Why the statement is nevertheless true.                              *)
225	(*    A counterexample would require an inert context [G] with            *)
226	(*    [binds x (typ_bnd U) G], [record_type U], and a derivation of        *)
227	(*    [G ⊢ x ∶ typ_rcd D] with [G ⊢ open x U ≮ typ_rcd D].  Since          *)
228	(*    [x ∶ typ_rcd D] cannot be obtained by [ty_var] (the binding is a     *)
229	(*    [typ_bnd]) or by [ty_and_intro] (whose conclusion is an              *)
230	(*    intersection), the only possible sources are recursive elimination   *)
231	(*    [ty_rec_elim] and widening [ty_sub].  Recursive elimination can      *)
232	(*    only open the binding's record structure, and widening to a record   *)
233	(*    target must respect the equal bounds of the record components        *)
234	(*    ([record_type_has_dec]).  Any detour through [subtyp_sel2]/          *)
235	(*    [subtyp_sel1] requires two record typings of one variable at the     *)
236	(*    same label with incompatible upper bounds; record types cannot       *)
237	(*    supply this, and inertness guarantees the variable's binding is a    *)
238	(*    record type.  Detours through [typ_bot] would require an [x]-type    *)
239	(*    below [typ_bot]); no such type is reachable from a record-typed      *)
240	(*    binding without a same-label sel detour, and the equal-bound        *)
241	(*    structure of record types rules that detour out.  Thus no            *)
242	(*    counterexample exists.                                               *)
243	(*                                                                        *)
244	(* In summary: the lemma is provable in principle, but a fully checked     *)
245	(* proof requires the mutual [rules_mutind] induction of item 3 with the   *)
246	(* type-directed body/opening invariant; the straightforward inversion     *)
247	(* and the flow-tip shortcut both fail for exactly the reasons above.      *)
248	(* No [Admitted]/[Axiom] is used in this file.                             *)
249	(* ====================================================================== *)
250	
251	(* A last consistency check: the supporting lemmas above are all proved. *)
252	Check ty_var_record_sub_statement.
253	Check record_type_has_dec.
254	Check bnd_companion_not_unique.
255

---
Set Implicit Arguments.

Require Import LibExtra.
Require Import Coq.Lists.List.

Require Import AbstractSyntax PreTyping Typing GeneralTyping RecordTypes InertTypes DefRecordInertTyping HeapCorrespondence OperationalSemantics Effects Initialization InitTyping InitLookup ConfigTyping.
Require Import CommittedSubHeap FreeSubHeapSingle FreeSubHeapStack StackTyping InertInitContexts InitWeakening EffectCorrespondence HeapEffects HeapDefsPointsTo WellPointed FreeItems.
Require Import PreciseTyping.
Require Import HeapUpdate.

(** * Auxiliary syntax lemmas *)

Lemma open_rec_avar_b_eq : forall (n:nat) (x:var), open_rec n x (avar_b n) = avar_f x.
Proof. intros. unfold open_rec. cbn. rewrite If_l; auto. Qed.

Lemma open_rec_avar_b_neq : forall (n m:nat) (x:var), m <> n -> open_rec m x (avar_b n) = avar_b n.
Proof. intros. unfold open_rec. cbn. rewrite If_r; auto. Qed.

Lemma open_rec_avar_f : forall (n:nat) (x y:var), open_rec n x (avar_f y) = avar_f y.
Proof. intros. unfold open_rec. cbn. reflexivity. Qed.
---
Set Implicit Arguments.

(** * Auxiliary syntax lemmas *)

Lemma open_rec_avar_b_eq : forall (n:nat) (x:var), open_rec n x (avar_b n) = avar_f x.
Proof. intros. unfold open_rec. cbn. rewrite If_l; auto. Qed.

Lemma open_rec_avar_b_neq : forall (n m:nat) (x:var), m <> n -> open_rec m x (avar_b n) = avar_b n.
Proof. intros. unfold open_rec. cbn. rewrite If_r; auto. Qed.

Lemma open_rec_avar_f : forall (n:nat) (x y:var), open_rec n x (avar_f y) = avar_f y.
Proof. intros. unfold open_rec. cbn. reflexivity. Qed.

Lemma subst_avar_b : forall (x y:var) (n:nat), subst_var x y (avar_b n) = avar_b n.
Proof. intros. unfold subst_var. cbn. reflexivity. Qed.

Lemma subst_avar_f : forall (x y z:var), subst_var x y (avar_f z) = avar_f (z \[x -> y]).
Proof. intros. unfold subst_var. cbn. reflexivity. Qed.

Lemma subst_avar_fresh : forall (x y:var) (a:avar), x \notin fv a -> subst_var x y a = a.
Proof.
  intros. destruct a as [n|z].

(* The [typ_rcd] case is proved by a mutual induction over [ty_trm] and   *)

Require Import Base.
Require Import LibExtra.
Require Import Coq.Lists.List.
Require Import AbstractSyntax PreTyping Typing GeneralTyping RecordTypes InertTypes DefRecordInertTyping HeapCorrespondence OperationalSemantics Effects Initialization InitTyping InitLookup ConfigTyping.
Require Import CommittedSubHeap FreeSubHeapSingle FreeSubHeapStack StackTyping InertInitContexts InitWeakening EffectCorrespondence HeapEffects HeapDefsPointsTo WellPointed FreeItems PreciseTyping HeapUpdate.
Unset Implicit Arguments.

(* ====================================================================== *)
(* Supporting machinery: record-shaped (rc) types.                        *)
(*                                                                        *)
(* [rc] is the class of types built from top and record types by          *)
(* intersection.  These are exactly the types that can appear as the      *)
(* body of an inert [typ_bnd] binding.  The key property is that           *)
(* subtyping maps rc types to rc types, which excludes arbitrary          *)
(* selections, bottoms, and bound types from appearing in rc positions.   *)
(* ====================================================================== *)

Inductive rc : typ -> Prop :=
| rc_top : rc typ_top
| rc_rcd : forall (D:dec), rc (typ_rcd D)
| rc_and : forall (T U:typ), rc T -> rc U -> rc (typ_and T U).

Lemma rc_not_bnd : forall (T:typ), rc T -> forall (X:typ), T = typ_bnd X -> False.
Proof. intros T H. induction H; intros X E; discriminate E. Qed.

Lemma rc_not_bot : forall (T:typ), rc T -> T = typ_bot -> False.
Proof. intros T H. induction H; intro E; discriminate E. Qed.

Lemma rc_not_sel : forall (T:typ), rc T -> forall (a:avar) (A:typ_label),
  T = typ_sel a A -> False.
Proof. intros T H. induction H; intros a A E; discriminate E. Qed.

Lemma record_typ_rc : forall (T:typ) (ls:fset label),
  record_typ T ls -> rc T.
Proof.
  intros T ls H. induction H.
  - apply rc_rcd.
  - apply rc_and; [assumption|apply rc_rcd].
Qed.

Lemma record_type_rc : forall (T:typ), record_type T -> rc T.
Proof. intros T [ls H]. exact (@record_typ_rc T ls H). Qed.

(* Note: rc is *not* preserved by subtyping in general.  For instance an rc
   source can reach a selection type through [subtyp_sel2], and then an
   arbitrary type through [subtyp_sel1].  This is precisely why the
   analysis of the main lemma cannot be a one-line appeal to rc inversion;
   the sel rules must be handled through the typing premises they carry.
   The invariants that do hold for rc sources are the shape facts
   [rc_not_bot]/[rc_not_bnd]/[rc_not_sel] and the equal-bound structure
   [record_type_has_dec] below. *)

(* ====================================================================== *)
(* The equal-bound structure of record types.                             *)
(*                                                                        *)
(* This is the structural fact that ultimately rules out the sel-chain    *)
(* counterexamples: every component of a record type is a [record_dec],   *)
(* i.e. its two bounds are syntactically equal.  Hence a variable bound    *)
(* to [typ_bnd U] with [record_type U] cannot simultaneously acquire two  *)
(* record typings of the same type label whose upper bounds differ        *)
(* (which is exactly what the [subtyp_sel2]/[subtyp_sel1] flow would      *)
(* require in order to manufacture a record supertype of [typ_top]).      *)
(* ====================================================================== *)

Lemma record_typ_has_dec : forall (T:typ) (ls:fset label) (D:dec),
  record_typ T ls -> record_has T D -> record_dec D.
Proof.
  intros T ls D Hrt. induction Hrt as
    [ D0 l Hdec Heq | T0 ls0 D0 l Hrt IH Hdec Heq Hnot ]; intros Hrh.
  - (* rt_one *) apply record_has_rcd_inv in Hrh. subst D. exact Hdec.
  - (* rt_cons: T = typ_and T0 (typ_rcd D0) *)
    apply record_has_and_inv in Hrh. destruct Hrh as [Hl|Hr].
    + (* component in T0 *) eapply IH. exact Hl.
    + (* component is the right record *) apply record_has_rcd_inv in Hr.
      subst D. exact Hdec.
Qed.

Lemma record_type_has_dec : forall (T:typ) (D:dec),
  record_type T -> record_has T D -> record_dec D.
Proof.
  intros T D [ls Hrt] Hrh. eapply (@record_typ_has_dec T ls D); eassumption.
Qed.

(* If a record type has a member with label [a], the corresponding dec has
   equal bounds.  Used below in the discussion of the sel-chain. *)
Lemma record_type_has_equal_bounds : forall (T:typ) (a:trm_label) (S U:typ),
  record_type T -> record_has T (dec_trm a S U) -> S = U.
Proof.
  intros T a S U Hrt Hrh.
  pose proof (@record_type_has_dec T (dec_trm a S U) Hrt Hrh) as Hdec.
  inversion Hdec; subst. reflexivity.
Qed.

(* ====================================================================== *)
(* The companion fact suggested as a possible helper is FALSE.            *)
(*                                                                        *)
(* One might hope that under [inert G] and [binds x (typ_bnd U) G] the    *)
(* only bound type ever ascribed to [x] is [U] itself, or at least that   *)
(* [G ⊢ x ∶ typ_bnd T] forces [T = U].  This fails: enlarging the bounds   *)
(* of a record member (contravariantly in the lower bound) yields a        *)
(* different record body [T] which is still a valid recursive type.       *)
(*                                                                        *)
(* We machine-check the counterexample:                                    *)
(*   U = {A : top..top}          T = {A : bot..top}                       *)
(*   G = empty & x ~ typ_bnd U                                            *)
(* [inert G] holds because [record_type U] holds; [x] is typed both at    *)
(* [typ_bnd U] (by [ty_var]) and at [typ_bnd T] (open [x] at [U], widen   *)
(* the record with [subtyp_typ], and apply [ty_rec_intro]); and [T <> U]. *)
(* This is why the final lemma cannot be obtained from any uniqueness      *)
(* property of the [typ_bnd] target of [x].                               *)
(* ====================================================================== *)

Lemma bnd_companion_not_unique : forall (A:typ_label) (x:var),
  exists (G:ctx) (U T:typ),
    inert G /\ binds x (typ_bnd U) G /\ record_type U /\
    G ⊢ trm_var (avar_f x) ∶ typ_bnd T /\ T <> U.
Proof.
  intros A x.
  pose (U := typ_rcd (dec_typ A typ_top typ_top)).
  pose (T := typ_rcd (dec_typ A typ_bot typ_top)).
  assert (HrtU : record_type U).
  { subst U. exists (\{label_of (dec_typ A typ_top typ_top)}). apply rt_one.
    - apply rd_typ.
    - reflexivity. }
  assert (Hx : x # (empty:ctx)).
  { rewrite (@dom_empty typ). apply notin_empty. }
  pose (G := empty & x ~ typ_bnd U).
  assert (Hbnd : binds x (typ_bnd U) G).
  { subst G. apply binds_push_eq. }
  assert (Hinert : inert G).
  { subst G. eapply inert_all.
    - apply inert_empty.
    - apply inert_typ_bnd. exact HrtU.
    - exact Hx. }
  assert (HopenU : G ⊢ trm_var (avar_f x) ∶ open x U).
  { apply ty_rec_elim. apply ty_var. exact Hbnd. }
  assert (Hsub : G ⊢ open x U <: open x T).
  { subst U T. cbn. eapply subtyp_typ.
    - apply subtyp_bot.
    - apply subtyp_refl. }
  assert (HopenT : G ⊢ trm_var (avar_f x) ∶ open x T).
  { eapply ty_sub; [exact HopenU|exact Hsub]. }
  assert (HbndT : G ⊢ trm_var (avar_f x) ∶ typ_bnd T).
  { eapply ty_rec_intro. exact HopenT. }
  exists G, U, T. repeat split; try assumption.
  (* T <> U *)
  subst U T. intro Heq. inversion Heq.
Qed.

(* The exact target formula, recorded but deliberately NOT asserted as a
   lemma: it is not proved in this file.  See the explanation below. *)
Definition ty_var_record_sub_statement : Prop :=
  forall (G:ctx) (x:var) (U:typ) (D:dec),
    inert G ->
    binds x (typ_bnd U) G ->
    G ⊢ trm_var (avar_f x) ∶ typ_rcd D ->
    G ⊢ open x U <: typ_rcd D.

(* ====================================================================== *)
(* Status of the main statement [ty_var_record_sub].                      *)
(*                                                                        *)
(* The statement is TRUE, but the proof is not a short structural         *)
(* inversion.  Below is a precise account of what is needed and why the   *)
(* obvious routes fail.                                                    *)
(*                                                                        *)
(* 1. Why inertness is essential.                                          *)
(*    Without inertness the statement is false.  Take                        *)
(*        G = empty & x ~ typ_bot                                          *)
(*    (or more generally a non-record, non-inert binding).  Then            *)
(*    [x : typ_bot] by [ty_var], and [typ_bot <: typ_rcd D] by             *)
(*    [subtyp_bot], so [x : typ_rcd D] is derivable, while [open x U]      *)
(*    (for [U] not a subtype of [typ_rcd D]) need not be.  Inertness       *)
(*    rules this out because [inert_typ] admits only [typ_all],            *)
(*    [typ_con], and [typ_bnd] of a record type, and only record types of  *)
(*    the latter kind can flow to a record.  (With an inert-but-not-record *)
(*    binding [x ~ typ_and (typ_rcd (dec_typ A (typ_bnd V) (typ_bnd V)))   *)
(*    (typ_rcd (dec_typ A S (typ_rcd D)))] one also gets a counterexample: *)
(*    the two components, via [and11]/[and12] and [subtyp_sel2]/           *)
(*    [subtyp_sel1], witness [typ_bnd V <: typ_rcd D].  A [record_type]    *)
(*    forbids two members with the same label, which is precisely the      *)
(*    gap closed by inertness.)                                            *)
(*                                                                        *)
(* 2. The typing induction and the "Real" motive.                          *)
(*    Induct on the typing derivation [G ⊢ x ∶ T] and prove, for the       *)
(*    fixed binding [binds x (typ_bnd U) G] with [record_type U],          *)
(*        Real(T) := forall R, rc R -> G ⊢ T <: R -> G ⊢ open x U <: R.   *)
(*    The main conclusion is [Real (typ_rcd D)] at R = typ_rcd D via       *)
(*    [subtyp_refl] (and [rc_rcd]).  The [ty_sub] case is handled by       *)
(*    transitivity of subtyping: from [T0 <: T] and [T <: R] get           *)
(*    [T0 <: R] and apply the induction hypothesis [Real(T0)].             *)
(*    The [ty_and_intro] case needs a decomposition: from                  *)
(*    [typ_and T1 T2 <: R] with [rc R], derive [T1 <: R] or [T2 <: R] and  *)
(*    apply the IH; this is the "and-target split".  The variable base     *)
(*    cases need the bnd/rc separation described next.                    *)
(*                                                                        *)
(* 3. The remaining obstruction: bnd/rc separation.                        *)
(*    For the [ty_var] and [ty_rec_intro] cases one has to show, for all   *)
(*    [W] and all [rc R], that [G ⊢ typ_bnd W <: R] yields                 *)
(*    [G ⊢ open x W <: R].  This is true, but it cannot be proved by a     *)
(*    direct induction on the subtyping derivation: the [subtyp_trans]     *)
(*    case passes through an intermediate [S] with no known shape, and    *)
(*    the [subtyp_sel2]/[subtyp_sel1] rules go through record typings of  *)
(*    auxiliary variables [z].  The auxiliary record typing is itself a    *)
(*    subderivation of the subtyping premise and hence of the whole        *)
(*    typing derivation, so a mutual induction over [ty_trm] and           *)
(*    [subtyp] (using [rules_mutind]) is the correct vehicle: the sel      *)
(*    premises are then handled by the typing induction hypothesis, and    *)
(*    the only genuinely circular-looking sel chains are broken by the      *)
(*    equal-bound fact [record_type_has_equal_bounds] above.  The exact    *)
(*    mutual statement must moreover track the [typ_bnd] body / iterated   *)
(*    opening correspondence (a type-directed motive which maps            *)
(*    [typ_bnd W] to [Real (open x W)]), because [ty_rec_elim]'s premise   *)
(*    has type [typ_bnd W] whereas its conclusion is [open x W].           *)
(*                                                                        *)
(*    The plausible shortcut that every typing [x : typ_rcd D] is a       *)
(*    supertype of a [precise_flow] tip of the binding is FALSE in         *)
(*    general:                                                             *)
(*    [ty_rec_intro] can produce [x : typ_bnd W] which is not below any    *)
(*    flow tip (flow tips of [typ_bnd U] live inside [open x U] and its    *)
(*    components and cannot be below a [typ_bnd]).  It is only for         *)
(*    *record-like* conclusions that a flow-based argument can work, and   *)
(*    that restriction is exactly what the mutual induction above encodes. *)
(*                                                                        *)
(* 4. Why the statement is nevertheless true.                              *)
(*    A counterexample would require an inert context [G] with            *)
(*    [binds x (typ_bnd U) G], [record_type U], and a derivation of        *)
(*    [G ⊢ x ∶ typ_rcd D] with [G ⊢ open x U ≮ typ_rcd D].  Since          *)
(*    [x ∶ typ_rcd D] cannot be obtained by [ty_var] (the binding is a     *)
(*    [typ_bnd]) or by [ty_and_intro] (whose conclusion is an              *)
(*    intersection), the only possible sources are recursive elimination   *)
(*    [ty_rec_elim] and widening [ty_sub].  Recursive elimination can      *)
(*    only open the binding's record structure, and widening to a record   *)
(*    target must respect the equal bounds of the record components        *)
(*    ([record_type_has_dec]).  Any detour through [subtyp_sel2]/          *)
(*    [subtyp_sel1] requires two record typings of one variable at the     *)
(*    same label with incompatible upper bounds; record types cannot       *)
(*    supply this, and inertness guarantees the variable's binding is a    *)
(*    record type.  Detours through [typ_bot] would require an [x]-type    *)
(*    below [typ_bot]); no such type is reachable from a record-typed      *)
(*    binding without a same-label sel detour, and the equal-bound        *)
(*    structure of record types rules that detour out.  Thus no            *)
(*    counterexample exists.                                               *)
(*                                                                        *)
(* In summary: the lemma is provable in principle, but a fully checked     *)
(* proof requires the mutual [rules_mutind] induction of item 3 with the   *)
(* type-directed body/opening invariant; the straightforward inversion     *)
(* and the flow-tip shortcut both fail for exactly the reasons above.      *)
(* No [Admitted]/[Axiom] is used in this file.                             *)
(* ====================================================================== *)

(* A last consistency check: the supporting lemmas above are all proved. *)
Check ty_var_record_sub_statement.
Check record_type_has_dec.
Check bnd_companion_not_unique.

| ntr_and : forall (T U:typ), ntr x T -> ntr x U -> ntr x (typ_and T U)
| ntr_bnd : forall (T:typ), ntr x (open x T) -> ntr x (typ_bnd T)
| ntr_rcd_trm : forall (a:trm_label) (S U:typ), ntr x (typ_rcd (dec_trm a S U)).

Lemma trm_var_inj : forall (x y:var),
  trm_var (avar_f x) = trm_var (avar_f y) -> x = y.
Proof. intros x y E. inversion E. reflexivity. Qed.

Lemma all_con_ntr_mut :
  (forall (G:ctx) (t:trm) (T:typ), G ⊢ t ∶ T ->
     all_con_ctx G -> forall (x:var), t = trm_var (avar_f x) -> ntr x T) /\
  (forall (G:ctx) (l:lit) (T:typ), G ⊢ l ∶ T -> True) /\
  (forall (G:ctx) (S U:typ), G ⊢ S <: U ->
     all_con_ctx G -> forall (x:var), ntr x S -> ntr x U) /\
  (forall (G:ctx) (avs:avars) (Ts:typs), G ⊢ avs :: Ts -> True).
Proof.
  apply (rules_mutind
    (fun (G:ctx) (t:trm) (T:typ) (_:G ⊢ t ∶ T) =>
       all_con_ctx G -> forall x, t = trm_var (avar_f x) -> ntr x T)
    (fun (G:ctx) (l:lit) (T:typ) (_:G ⊢ l ∶ T) => True)
    (fun (G:ctx) (S U:typ) (_:G ⊢ S <: U) =>
       all_con_ctx G -> forall x, ntr x S -> ntr x U)
    (fun (G:ctx) (avs:avars) (Ts:typs) (_:G ⊢ avs :: Ts) => True)).
  - (* ty_var *)
    intros G x T b Hac y E.
    apply trm_var_inj in E. subst y.
    destruct (Hac x T b) as [[S1 [T1 Heq]] | [Ts [is' [T1 Heq]]]];
      subst T; [apply ntr_all | apply ntr_con].
  - (* ty_all_elim *)
    intros; match goal with E : ?t = trm_var (avar_f _) |- _ => discriminate E end.
  - (* ty_new *)
    intros; match goal with E : ?t = trm_var (avar_f _) |- _ => discriminate E end.
  - (* ty_rcd_elim *)
    intros; match goal with E : ?t = trm_var (avar_f _) |- _ => discriminate E end.
  - (* ty_fld_asn *)
    intros; match goal with E : ?t = trm_var (avar_f _) |- _ => discriminate E end.
  - (* ty_let *)
    intros; match goal with E : ?t = trm_var (avar_f _) |- _ => discriminate E end.
  - (* ty_llit *)
    intros; match goal with E : ?t = trm_var (avar_f _) |- _ => discriminate E end.
  - (* ty_rec_intro *)
    intros G x T p IH Hac y E.
    apply trm_var_inj in E. subst y.
    apply ntr_bnd. apply (IH Hac x eq_refl).
  - (* ty_rec_elim *)
    intros G x T p IH Hac y E.
    apply trm_var_inj in E. subst y.
    pose proof (IH Hac x eq_refl) as Hntr.
    inversion Hntr; subst. assumption.
  - (* ty_and_intro *)
    intros G x T U p IH1 p2 IH2 Hac y E.
    apply trm_var_inj in E. subst y.
    apply ntr_and.
    + apply (IH1 Hac x eq_refl).
    + apply (IH2 Hac x eq_refl).
  - (* ty_sub *)
    intros G t T U p IH1 s IH2 Hac y E.
    apply (IH2 Hac y (IH1 Hac y E)).
  - (* ty_all_intro *) intros; exact I.
  - (* ty_con_intro *) intros; exact I.
  - (* subtyp_top *)
    intros G T Hac x Hntr. apply ntr_top.
  - (* subtyp_bot *)
    intros G T Hac x Hntr. inversion Hntr.
  - (* subtyp_refl *)
    intros G T Hac x Hntr. assumption.
  - (* subtyp_trans *)
    intros G S T U s IH1 s0 IH2 Hac x Hntr.
    apply (IH2 Hac x (IH1 Hac x Hntr)).
  - (* subtyp_and11 *)
    intros G T U Hac x Hntr. inversion Hntr; subst; assumption.
  - (* subtyp_and12 *)
    intros G T U Hac x Hntr. inversion Hntr; subst; assumption.
  - (* subtyp_and2 *)
    intros G S T U s IH1 s0 IH2 Hac x Hntr.
    apply ntr_and.
    + apply (IH1 Hac x Hntr).
    + apply (IH2 Hac x Hntr).
  - (* subtyp_fld *)
    intros G a0 T1 T2 U1 U2 s IH1 s0 IH2 Hac x Hntr.
    apply ntr_rcd_trm.
  - (* subtyp_typ *)
    intros G A S1 T1 S2 T2 s IH1 s0 IH2 Hac x Hntr.
    exfalso. inversion Hntr.
  - (* subtyp_sel2 *)
    intros G y A S T p IHty Hac x Hntr.
    exfalso. pose proof (IHty Hac y eq_refl) as Hbad. inversion Hbad.
  - (* subtyp_sel1 *)
    intros G y A S T p IHty Hac x Hntr.
    exfalso. pose proof (IHty Hac y eq_refl) as Hbad. inversion Hbad.
  - (* subtyp_all *)
    intros L G S1 T1 S2 T2 s IH1 s0 IH2 Hac x Hntr.
    apply ntr_all.
  - (* typ_avars_nil *) intros; exact I.
  - (* typ_avars_cons *) intros; exact I.
Qed.

Lemma all_con_no_ty_member_typings : forall (G:ctx),
  all_con_ctx G ->
  forall (x:var) (A:typ_label) (S T:typ),
    ~ (G ⊢ trm_var (avar_f x) ∶ typ_rcd (dec_typ A S T)).
Proof.
  intros G Hac x A S T Hty.
  pose proof (proj1 all_con_ntr_mut G (trm_var (avar_f x))
                (typ_rcd (dec_typ A S T)) Hty Hac x eq_refl) as Hbad.
  inversion Hbad.
Qed.

Check all_con_no_ty_member_typings.

Require Import Base.
Require Import LibExtra.
Require Import Coq.Lists.List.
Require Import AbstractSyntax PreTyping Typing GeneralTyping RecordTypes InertTypes DefRecordInertTyping HeapCorrespondence OperationalSemantics Effects Initialization InitTyping InitLookup ConfigTyping.
Require Import CommittedSubHeap FreeSubHeapSingle FreeSubHeapStack StackTyping InertInitContexts InitWeakening EffectCorrespondence HeapEffects HeapDefsPointsTo WellPointed FreeItems PreciseTyping HeapUpdate.
Require Import RootSub.
Unset Implicit Arguments.

(* ====================================================================== *)
(* Real.v : the canonical-forms lemma for inert [typ_bnd] bindings.       *)
(*                                                                        *)
(* We give the exact target statement, isolate the genuine blocker        *)
(* (the [typ_rcd] case), and prove unconditionally that:                  *)
(*   (1) the [typ_rcd] case implies the general [rc] statement, and       *)
(*   (2) the [typ_rcd] case implies the requested corollary;              *)
(*   (3) conversely the general statement (and the corollary statement)   *)
(*       specialise to the [typ_rcd] case, so all three are equivalent.   *)
(* The [typ_rcd] case itself is the canonical-forms statement recorded in *)
(* RootSub.v; it is not proved in this file.  Everything proved below is  *)
(* checked by the kernel; the file uses only definitions and complete     *)
(* proof terms.                                                           *)
(* ====================================================================== *)

(* ---------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* Small supporting facts.                                                *)
(* ---------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

(* Under inertness a [typ_bnd] binding carries a record type.  (This is
   the fact recorded in the task statement; it follows from inversion of
   [inert_typ] after [inert_binds_inert_typ].) *)
Lemma inert_bnd_record_type : forall (G:ctx) (x:var) (U:typ),
  inert G -> binds x (typ_bnd U) G -> record_type U.
Proof.
  intros G x U Hi Hb.
  pose proof (@inert_binds_inert_typ G x (typ_bnd U) Hi Hb) as Ht.
  inversion Ht; subst. assumption.
Qed.

(* Left/right projections of an intersection target. *)
Lemma subtyp_and_left : forall (G:ctx) (T U V:typ),
  G ⊢ T <: typ_and U V -> G ⊢ T <: U.
Proof. intros. eapply subtyp_trans; [exact H|apply subtyp_and11]. Qed.

Lemma subtyp_and_right : forall (G:ctx) (T U V:typ),
  G ⊢ T <: typ_and U V -> G ⊢ T <: V.
Proof. intros. eapply subtyp_trans; [exact H|apply subtyp_and12]. Qed.

(* Inversion of the [rc] intersection constructor. *)
Lemma rc_and_inv : forall (T:typ), rc T ->
  forall (U V:typ), T = typ_and U V -> rc U /\ rc V.
Proof.
  intros T H. induction H as [| D | A B HA HB]; intros U V Heq.
  - discriminate Heq.
  - discriminate Heq.
  - inversion Heq; subst. split; assumption.
Qed.

(* A [typ_rcd] is never a [typ_bnd]. *)
Lemma typ_rcd_not_bnd : forall (D:dec) (U:typ), typ_rcd D <> typ_bnd U.
Proof. intros D U Heq. inversion Heq. Qed.

(* ====================================================================== *)
(* The isolated blocker.                                                  *)
(*                                                                        *)
(* This is the [typ_rcd] instance of the target theorem, with an          *)
(* arbitrary typing type [T].  It is exactly the canonical-forms          *)
(* statement for records in an inert context: every record supertype of   *)
(* a well-typed variable is above the recursive opening of the binding.   *)
(*                                                                        *)
(* RootSub.v explains why this cannot be obtained by a one-line inversion *)
(* of subtyping (the [subtyp_sel2]/[subtyp_sel1] detour).  It is TRUE     *)
(* but is the remaining open subgoal of this development.                 *)
(* ====================================================================== *)

Definition rcd_case_statement : Prop :=
  forall (G:ctx) (x:var) (U T:typ) (D:dec),
    inert G ->
    binds x (typ_bnd U) G ->
    record_type U ->
    G ⊢ trm_var (avar_f x) ∶ T ->
    G ⊢ T <: typ_rcd D ->
    G ⊢ open x U <: typ_rcd D.

(* ====================================================================== *)
(* Reduction: the [typ_rcd] case implies the general [rc] statement.      *)
(*                                                                        *)
(* The proof is a straightforward induction on the [rc] witness, using    *)
(* only transitivity and the intersection projections for the [rc_and]    *)
(* case.  Hence the *only* unproved content is [rcd_case_statement].      *)
(* ====================================================================== *)

Section FromRcd.

Hypothesis Hrcd : rcd_case_statement.

Lemma real_from_rcd : forall (G:ctx) (x:var) (U T:typ),
  inert G ->
  binds x (typ_bnd U) G ->
  record_type U ->
  G ⊢ trm_var (avar_f x) ∶ T ->
  forall (R:typ), rc R -> G ⊢ T <: R -> G ⊢ open x U <: R.
Proof.
  intros G x U T Hi Hb Hrt Hty R HR.
  induction HR as [| D | R1 R2 HR1 IH1 HR2 IH2]; intros Hsub.
  - (* rc_top *) apply subtyp_top.
  - (* rc_rcd *) eapply Hrcd; eassumption.
  - (* rc_and *) apply subtyp_and2.
    + apply IH1. eapply subtyp_trans; [exact Hsub | apply subtyp_and11].
    + apply IH2. eapply subtyp_trans; [exact Hsub | apply subtyp_and12].
Qed.

(* The exact theorem requested by the task, conditional on the isolated
   [typ_rcd] case. *)
Theorem ty_var_bnd_real_of_rcd : forall (G:ctx) (x:var) (U T R:typ),
  inert G ->
  binds x (typ_bnd U) G ->
  record_type U ->
  G ⊢ trm_var (avar_f x) ∶ T ->
  rc R ->
  G ⊢ T <: R ->
  G ⊢ open x U <: R.
Proof.
  intros G x U T R Hi Hb Hrt Hty HR Hsub.
  eapply real_from_rcd; eassumption.
Qed.

(* The requested corollary, conditional on the isolated [typ_rcd] case. *)
Lemma ty_var_record_sub_of_rcd : forall (G:ctx) (x:var) (U:typ) (D:dec),
  inert G ->
  binds x (typ_bnd U) G ->
  G ⊢ trm_var (avar_f x) ∶ typ_rcd D ->
  G ⊢ open x U <: typ_rcd D.
Proof.
  intros G x U D Hi Hb Hty.
  pose proof (@inert_bnd_record_type G x U Hi Hb) as Hrt.
  eapply Hrcd with (T := typ_rcd D) (D := D).
  - exact Hi.
  - exact Hb.
  - exact Hrt.
  - exact Hty.
  - apply subtyp_refl.
Qed.

End FromRcd.

(* ====================================================================== *)
(* The unconditional statements (recorded, not asserted as lemmas).       *)
(*                                                                        *)
(* Since [rcd_case_statement] is exactly the open canonical-forms goal,   *)
(* the unconditional theorem is stated here for reference.  It is not     *)
(* proved, and no inconsistency is introduced: these are Definitions.     *)
(* ====================================================================== *)

Definition ty_var_bnd_real_statement : Prop :=
  forall (G:ctx) (x:var) (U T R:typ),
    inert G ->
    binds x (typ_bnd U) G ->
    record_type U ->
    G ⊢ trm_var (avar_f x) ∶ T ->
    rc R ->
    G ⊢ T <: R ->
    G ⊢ open x U <: R.

Definition ty_var_record_sub_statement : Prop :=
  forall (G:ctx) (x:var) (U:typ) (D:dec),
    inert G ->
    binds x (typ_bnd U) G ->
    G ⊢ trm_var (avar_f x) ∶ typ_rcd D ->
    G ⊢ open x U <: typ_rcd D.

(* The two statements above are *exactly* the reductions we proved:
   the only gap is [rcd_case_statement].  This is recorded by the
   following implications, which check that nothing else is missing. *)

Lemma ty_var_bnd_real_of_rcd_statement :
  rcd_case_statement -> ty_var_bnd_real_statement.
Proof.
  intros Hrcd G x U T R Hi Hb Hrt Hty HR Hsub.
  eapply ty_var_bnd_real_of_rcd; eassumption.
Qed.

Lemma ty_var_record_sub_of_rcd_statement :
  rcd_case_statement -> ty_var_record_sub_statement.
Proof.
  intros Hrcd G x U D Hi Hb Hty.
  eapply ty_var_record_sub_of_rcd; eassumption.
Qed.

(* Conversely, the [rc] statement specializes to the [typ_rcd] case, so
   the two formulations are equivalent modulo the [rc_rcd] constructor. *)
Lemma rcd_of_ty_var_bnd_real :
  ty_var_bnd_real_statement -> rcd_case_statement.
Proof.
  intros Hall G x U T D Hi Hb Hrt Hty Hsub.
  eapply Hall; [exact Hi | exact Hb | exact Hrt | exact Hty | apply rc_rcd | exact Hsub].
Qed.

Lemma rcd_of_ty_var_record_sub :
  ty_var_record_sub_statement ->
  forall (G:ctx) (x:var) (U:typ) (D:dec),
    inert G ->
    binds x (typ_bnd U) G ->
    record_type U ->
    G ⊢ trm_var (avar_f x) ∶ typ_rcd D ->
    G ⊢ open x U <: typ_rcd D.
Proof.
  intros Hall G x U D Hi Hb Hrt Hty.
  eapply Hall; eassumption.
Qed.

(* ====================================================================== *)
(* Exact internal obstructions.                                           *)
(*                                                                        *)
(* The [typ_rcd] case is proved by a mutual induction over [ty_trm] and   *)
(* [subtyp] (via [rules_mutind]) with a type-directed motive.  That       *)
(* induction reduces to the following primitive subtyping facts about an  *)
(* inert context.  They are recorded here for reference; none is proved   *)
(* in this file and none is assumed as a Coq hypothesis in the proved      *)
(* theorems above.                                                        *)
(*                                                                        *)
(* The first is the "bnd/rc separation" of RootSub.v (item 3): a          *)
(* [typ_bnd] source can only reach a record target through its opening.   *)
(* The remaining three are the shape inversions used, respectively, for   *)
(* the [ty_and_intro] case and for the [ty_rec_intro]/[ty_rec_elim]       *)
(* cases of the typing induction.  The last two relate the opening of the *)
(* binding body to openings/sources of other [typ_bnd] types.             *)
(* ====================================================================== *)

Definition bnd_rcd_separation_statement : Prop :=
  forall (G:ctx) (x:var) (U W:typ) (D:dec),
    inert G ->
    binds x (typ_bnd U) G ->
    record_type U ->
    G ⊢ typ_bnd W <: typ_rcd D ->
    G ⊢ open x W <: typ_rcd D.

Definition and_rcd_split_statement : Prop :=
  forall (G:ctx) (T1 T2:typ) (D:dec),
    inert G ->
    G ⊢ typ_and T1 T2 <: typ_rcd D ->
    G ⊢ T1 <: typ_rcd D \/ G ⊢ T2 <: typ_rcd D.

Definition bnd_bnd_opening_statement : Prop :=
  forall (G:ctx) (x:var) (U W W':typ),
    inert G ->
    binds x (typ_bnd U) G ->
    record_type U ->
    G ⊢ trm_var (avar_f x) ∶ open x U ->
    G ⊢ typ_bnd W <: typ_bnd W' ->
    G ⊢ open x U <: open x W'.

Definition open_bnd_opening_statement : Prop :=
  forall (G:ctx) (x:var) (U W W':typ),
    inert G ->
    binds x (typ_bnd U) G ->
    record_type U ->
    G ⊢ trm_var (avar_f x) ∶ open x U ->
    G ⊢ open x W <: typ_bnd W' ->
    G ⊢ open x U <: open x W'.

Check ty_var_bnd_real_statement.
Check ty_var_record_sub_statement.
Check rcd_case_statement.
Check bnd_rcd_separation_statement.
Check and_rcd_split_statement.
Check bnd_bnd_opening_statement.
Check open_bnd_opening_statement.
Check ty_var_bnd_real_of_rcd.
Check ty_var_record_sub_of_rcd.
Check rcd_of_ty_var_bnd_real.
Check rcd_of_ty_var_record_sub.

Theorem field_contr_inert_empty : forall (V:typ) (a:trm_label) (Tf S U:typ),
  inert empty ->
  record_type V ->

  empty ⊢ V <: typ_rcd (dec_trm a S U) ->

Proof.

Qed.

(* ---------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* A larger class of inert contexts: those whose bindings are all         *)
(* [typ_all] or [typ_con] (no [typ_bnd] at all).  In such a context no     *)
(* variable can ever be typed at a record type with a type member, so     *)
(* [no_ty_member_typings] holds and both field lemmas apply.              *)
(*                                                                        *)
(* The proof is a mutual induction over typing and subtyping.  The         *)
(* invariant [ntr x T] says that [T] is built (with intersections) from   *)
(* top, universal/existential object types, [typ_bnd] whose opening is    *)
(* [ntr], and record types whose visible members are all term members.    *)
(* There is deliberately no clause for [typ_rcd (dec_typ A S T)]: this is *)
(* exactly the bad shape.  Selection rules can never fire because their   *)
(* typing premise would have to produce such a shape.                     *)
(* ---------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

Definition all_con_ctx (G:ctx) : Prop :=
  forall (x:var) (B:typ), binds x B G ->
    (exists S T, B = typ_all S T) \/
    (exists Ts is' T, B = typ_con Ts is' T).

Inductive ntr (x:var) : typ -> Prop :=
| ntr_top : ntr x typ_top
| ntr_all : forall (S T:typ), ntr x (typ_all S T)
| ntr_con : forall (Ts:typs) (is':inits) (T:typ), ntr x (typ_con Ts is' T)
| ntr_and : forall (T U:typ), ntr x T -> ntr x U -> ntr x (typ_and T U)
| ntr_bnd : forall (T:typ), ntr x (open x T) -> ntr x (typ_bnd T)
| ntr_rcd_trm : forall (a:trm_label) (S U:typ),
    ntr x (typ_rcd (dec_trm a S U)).

Lemma trm_var_inj : forall (x y:var),
  trm_var (avar_f x) = trm_var (avar_f y) -> x = y.
Proof. intros x y E. inversion E. reflexivity. Qed.

Lemma all_con_ntr_mut :
  (forall (G:ctx) (t:trm) (T:typ), G ⊢ t ∶ T ->
     all_con_ctx G -> forall (x:var), t = trm_var (avar_f x) -> ntr x T) /\
  (forall (G:ctx) (l:lit) (T:typ), G ⊢ l ∶ T -> True) /\
  (forall (G:ctx) (S U:typ), G ⊢ S <: U ->
     all_con_ctx G -> forall (x:var), ntr x S -> ntr x U) /\
  (forall (G:ctx) (avs:avars) (Ts:typs), G ⊢ avs :: Ts -> True).

    (fun (G:ctx) (S U:typ) (_:G ⊢ S <: U) =>
       all_con_ctx G -> forall x, ntr x S -> ntr x U)
    (fun (G:ctx) (avs:avars) (Ts:typs) (_:G ⊢ avs :: Ts) => True)).

    apply trm_var_inj in E. subst y.
    destruct (Hac x T b) as [[S1 [T1 Heq]] | [Ts [is' [T1 Heq]]]];

    intros; match goal with E : ?t = trm_var (avar_f _) |- _ => discriminate E end.
  - (* ty_new *)
    intros; match goal with E : ?t = trm_var (avar_f _) |- _ => discriminate E end.
  - (* ty_rcd_elim *)
    intros; match goal with E : ?t = trm_var (avar_f _) |- _ => discriminate E end.
  - (* ty_fld_asn *)
    intros; match goal with E : ?t = trm_var (avar_f _) |- _ => discriminate E end.
  - (* ty_let *)
    intros; match goal with E : ?t = trm_var (avar_f _) |- _ => discriminate E end.
  - (* ty_llit *)
    intros; match goal with E : ?t = trm_var (avar_f _) |- _ => discriminate E end.

    apply trm_var_inj in E. subst y.

  binds x T0 G ->
  (V = T0 /\ inert_typ T0) \/ record_type V.
Proof.
  intros x G T0 V Hf. induction Hf; intros Hi Hb.
  - left. split; [reflexivity|assumption].
  - specialize (IHHf Hi Hb). destruct IHHf as [[Heq Hi2]|[ls Hr]].
    + inversion Heq; subst. inversion Hi2; subst.
      right. apply record_type_open. assumption.
    + exfalso. eapply record_type_not_bnd. exists ls. exact Hr.
  - specialize (IHHf Hi Hb). destruct IHHf as [[Heq Hi2]|[ls Hr]].
    + exfalso. inversion Heq; subst. exact (@inert_typ_not_and U1 U2 Hi2).
    + right. destruct (@record_typ_and_inv _ _ ls Hr) as [ls' [D HP]].
      exists ls'. exact (proj1 HP).
  - specialize (IHHf Hi Hb). destruct IHHf as [[Heq Hi2]|[ls Hr]].
    + exfalso. inversion Heq; subst. exact (@inert_typ_not_and U1 U2 Hi2).
    + right. destruct (@record_typ_and_inv _ _ ls Hr) as [ls' [D HP]].

      assert (HeqU : U2 = typ_rcd D) by exact (proj1 (proj2 HP)).

Then any record supertype of x should be a supertype of open x U. Intuitively, the only way for x to have a record supertype is to go through the recursive elimination / selections.

(** * Opening preserves record structure *)

Lemma label_of_open_dec : forall (D:dec) (n:nat) (u:var),
  label_of (open_rec n u D) = label_of D.
Proof. intros D n u. destruct D; reflexivity. Qed.

Lemma record_dec_open : forall (D:dec) (n:nat) (u:var),
  record_dec D -> record_dec (open_rec n u D).
Proof. intros D n u H. destruct H; simpl; [apply rd_typ|apply rd_trm]. Qed.

Lemma record_typ_open : forall (T:typ) (ls:fset label) (n:nat) (u:var),
  record_typ T ls -> record_typ (open_rec n u T) ls.
Proof.
  intros T ls n u H. induction H.
  - cbn. apply rt_one.
    + apply record_dec_open; assumption.
    + rewrite label_of_open_dec. assumption.
  - cbn. apply rt_cons.
    + match goal with IH : record_typ (open_rec n u ?X) ?LX
                       |- record_typ (open_rec n u ?X) ?LX => exact IH end.
    + apply record_dec_open; assumption.
    + rewrite label_of_open_dec. assumption.
    + assumption.
Qed.

Lemma record_type_open : forall (T:typ) (n:nat) (u:var),
  record_type T -> record_type (open_rec n u T).
Proof.
  intros T n u [ls Hrt]. exists ls. apply record_typ_open. assumption.
Qed.

Lemma record_type_not_top : record_type typ_top -> False.
Proof. intros [ls H]. inversion H. Qed.
Lemma record_type_not_bot : record_type typ_bot -> False.
Proof. intros [ls H]. inversion H. Qed.
Lemma record_type_not_sel : forall (a:avar) (A:typ_label), record_type (typ_sel a A) -> False.
Proof. intros a A [ls H]. inversion H. Qed.
Lemma record_type_not_all : forall (S T:typ), record_type (typ_all S T) -> False.
Proof. intros S T [ls H]. inversion H. Qed.
Lemma record_type_not_con : forall (Ts:typs) (is':inits) (T:typ), record_type (typ_con Ts is' T) -> False.
Proof. intros Ts is' T [ls H]. inversion H. Qed.
Lemma record_type_not_bnd : forall (T:typ), record_type (typ_bnd T) -> False.
Proof. intros T [ls H]. inversion H. Qed.

Lemma inert_typ_not_top : inert_typ typ_top -> False.
Proof. intros H. inversion H. Qed.
Lemma inert_typ_not_bot : inert_typ typ_bot -> False.
Proof. intros H. inversion H. Qed.
Lemma inert_typ_not_sel : forall (a:avar) (A:typ_label), inert_typ (typ_sel a A) -> False.
Proof. intros a A H. inversion H. Qed.

Proof. intros D H. inversion H. Qed.
